guide.what: Words have ending sounds as well as beginning sounds. Listen carefully to the last sound: bed ends in d, drum ends in m, sun ends in n.
steps: Say a word and stretch the last sound: suuunnn.
Play 'I spy something that ends in m'.
Clap on the last sound of each word.
home: Find five things at home that end in n.
Write a list of d words with your child.
guide.watch: m and n sound alike at the end. Ask your child to look at your lips: lips close for m, stay open for n.

title: Tanka poems Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 English practice on tanka poems, from "What Is a Tanka?" to "Draw Your Poem". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a tanka poem is.
Count syllables in words.
Know the 5-7-5-7-7 pattern.
Read and understand a tanka.
Find describing words in a poem.
Choose words for a nature poem.
Use describing words in poems.
Complete a tanka.
Write a tanka poem.
Illustrate a poem.

guide.what: A tanka is a 5-line poem from Japan, often about nature. The lines have 5, 7, 5, 7 and 7 syllables (beats).
steps: Clap syllables in family names.
Go outside and list three things you see, hear and feel.
Read the poem aloud together, clapping each beat.
home: Write a tanka about winter in Lahore.
Make a poem card for a grandparent.
guide.watch: Counting beats is hard at first. It is fine if a line is one beat off. The ideas matter more.

title: Writing a story Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 English practice on writing a story, from "Every Story Has Three Parts" to "Check and Draw". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a story has a beginning, middle and end.
Choose a story opening.
Find the character, setting and problem.
Put story events in order.
Use time words to join ideas.
Describe a character's feelings.
Add sense words to a story.
Plan a story before writing.
Write a short story with a beginning, middle and end.
Check own writing.

guide.what: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end. Good stories tell who, where and what happened, use joining words like first, next and then, and describe feelings and senses.
steps: After reading, ask: who, where, what was the problem?
Tell a story together, taking turns to add a sentence.
Let your child draw first, then write.
home: Write a story about a family trip.
Make a tiny book with four pages.
guide.watch: Young writers often stop at the middle. Ask: 'And how did it end?'

title: Number names to 20 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on number names to 20, from "Number Names 0 to 10" to "Write Them All". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read and write number names to 10.
Read and write number names 11 to 20.
Match number names to numbers.
Match numbers and number names.
Spell number names correctly.
See the pattern in teen numbers.
Count objects and write the number name.
Order number names.
Use number names in word problems.
Write number names neatly.

guide.what: Every number has a name: 0 zero, 1 one, up to 20 twenty. Teen numbers are 10 and some more: thirteen is 10 and 3.
steps: Read number names on price tags and clocks together.
Write number names on cards and play snap.
Spell one number name aloud each day.
home: Count steps on the stairs and say the names.
Find number names in a story book.
guide.watch: Twelve, fifteen and twenty are tricky spellings. Practise them more.

title: Comparing numbers Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on comparing numbers, from "More or Less?" to "Make It True". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare two numbers using more and less.
Use the greater than and less than signs.
Use the equals sign when numbers are the same.
Find the bigger of two numbers.
Compare groups of objects.
Order numbers to 20.
Find the biggest and smallest number in a set.
Find one more and one less.
Compare numbers in word problems.
Choose numbers that fit a comparison.

guide.what: We compare numbers to see which is greater, less or equal. The signs are > (greater than), < (less than) and = (equal to). The open side faces the bigger number.
steps: Compare two piles of chickpeas: which has more?
Draw a crocodile mouth on a card and use it between numbers.
Compare ages of family members.
home: Compare prices at a shop.
Roll two dice and say which number is bigger.
guide.watch: Children write > when they mean <. Say it aloud: 'The crocodile eats the bigger number.'

title: Adding and taking away stories Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on adding and taking away stories, from "Story Sums" to "Exit Ticket". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Solve addition stories within 10.
Solve subtraction stories within 10.
Choose the right operation.
Add and subtract on a number line.
Use a fact family of 3 numbers.
Find a missing number in a sum.
Use money in word problems.
Link maths and healthy eating.
Make up a word problem.
Check addition and subtraction within 10.

guide.what: Story sums use words. 'More', 'in all' and 'altogether' mean add. 'Left', 'flew away' and 'ate' mean take away. A number line helps: hop forward to add and back to take away.
steps: Turn snack time into story sums: 'You have 5 grapes and eat 2...'
Act out stories with toys.
Ask your child to make up a story for 4 + 3.
home: Play shop with coins and price tags.
Count cars that pass and how many turn away.
guide.watch: Children add every time they see two numbers. Ask: 'Did it get bigger or smaller?' before they solve.

Name the two groups: vertebrates and invertebrates.
Sort animals into vertebrates and invertebrates.
Sort animals into two groups.
Know that some invertebrates have soft bodies and some have hard shells.
Check facts about vertebrates and invertebrates.

Reflect on what you learned about backbones.
Link animals to their body features.
Use what you learned about backbones.

guide.what: Animals can be sorted into two groups. Vertebrates have a backbone (fish, frogs, snakes, birds, cows, people). Invertebrates have no backbone (worms, snails, insects, spiders, octopus).
steps: Feel your child's backbone together and count a few bumps.
Look for small creatures in the garden and ask: backbone or not?
Sort toy animals into two piles.
home: Look at a fish bone at dinner and talk about the backbone.
Watch a snail move slowly on a leaf.
guide.watch: Children often think a shell is a backbone. A snail's shell is outside its soft body; it is not a backbone.

title: Animal groups Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on animal groups, from "Groups of Animals" to "My Favourite Animal". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that scientists sort animals into groups.
Describe mammals.
Describe birds.
Describe fish.
Describe reptiles.
Describe amphibians.
Describe insects.
Classify animals into groups.
Check what you know about animal groups.
Describe an animal and its group.

guide.what: Animals are sorted into groups. Mammals have fur and feed babies milk. Birds have feathers and lay eggs. Fish live in water and breathe with gills. Reptiles have dry scaly skin. Amphibians live in water and on land. Insects have six legs and no backbone.
steps: Look at animals at the zoo or on TV and ask: which group?
Play 20 questions: Does it have feathers? Does it live in water?
Make a group chart with animal pictures from magazines.
home: Visit a zoo or farm and sort the animals you see.
Draw one animal from each group.
guide.watch: A whale lives in water but is a mammal, not a fish. A bat flies but is a mammal, not a bird.

words: live in water and on land

title: Parts of a plant Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on parts of a plant, from "Parts of a Plant" to "Draw and Label". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the main parts of a plant.
Describe what roots do.
Describe what a stem does.
Describe what leaves do.
Describe what flowers, fruit and seeds do.
Match each job to a plant part.
Know that we eat different plant parts.
Know what a plant needs to grow.
Observe how a seed grows.
Draw and label the parts of a plant.

guide.what: A plant has roots, a stem, leaves and flowers, and many grow fruit with seeds. Roots take in water, the stem carries it up, leaves make food using sunlight, and flowers make seeds.
steps: Pull out a weed and look at its roots together.
At the market, ask: which part of the plant is this?
Put a white flower in coloured water and watch the petals change.
home: Grow a bean in a jar.
Collect three different leaves and compare them.
guide.watch: Children think plants eat soil. Plants make their own food in their leaves using sunlight; soil gives water and nutrients.

title: Learning at school Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on learning at school, from "My School" to "I Love My School". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that school is a place to learn and make friends.
Name school helpers and what they do.
Explain why the principal is important.
Name places in school and what happens there.
Know why schools have rules.
Compare KG and Grade 1.
Know that we learn in many places.
Recall the main ideas about school.
Sequence a school day.
Describe your own school.

guide.what: School is a place to learn, make friends and follow rules. The principal, teachers, librarian, nurse, guard and cleaners all help. We learn at school, at home and everywhere around us.
steps: Ask your child to name everyone who helps at school.
Talk about one school rule and why it matters.
Compare what KG was like with Grade 1.
home: Walk past the school and name each building.
Write a thank-you card to a school helper.
guide.watch: Rules can feel like 'no' words. Talk about how each rule keeps someone safe or makes things fair.

title: Days, weeks and the calendar Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on days, weeks and the calendar, from "Days of the Week" to "Special Days". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Say the days of the week in order.
Find the day before and after.
Sort days into weekdays and weekend.
Say the months of the year in order.
Read dates on a calendar.
Know facts about days, weeks and months.
Use yesterday, today and tomorrow.
Describe a weekly routine.
Use the calendar to solve problems.
Link special days to months.

guide.what: A week has 7 days: 5 weekdays and 2 weekend days. A year has 12 months. A calendar shows the days and dates of each month.
steps: Say the days of the week each morning at breakfast.
Hang a calendar and cross off each day.
Mark family birthdays on the calendar together.
home: Count the days until a special event.
Sing the days of the week to a simple tune.
guide.watch: Children mix up 'yesterday' and 'tomorrow'. Use them every day: 'Yesterday we went to Nani's. Tomorrow is school.'

title: Data all around us Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on data all around us, from "What Is Data?" to "Data Detective". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that data is information we collect.
Collect data with tallies.
Read a simple pictogram.
Use labels to organise data.
Collect and record data.
Know that data can be numbers, words or pictures.
Show data in a pictogram.
Write clear survey questions.
Know that many jobs use data.
Use data to answer questions.

guide.what: Data is information: numbers, words or pictures. We collect it by counting, asking and measuring, and organise it with tallies, charts and labels. AI needs data to learn.
steps: Count cars by colour on a drive.
Make a tally of family favourite foods.
Read the weather chart together.
home: Survey family members and draw a pictogram.
Label boxes when tidying toys.
guide.watch: Show that bad data gives bad results: if you only ask boys, you do not know what girls like.

title: How AI learns from examples Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on how ai learns from examples, from "Training With Examples" to "Think About It". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI is trained with labelled examples.
Label data for training.
Know that more and varied examples help AI learn.
Explain why AI makes mistakes.
Plan a set of training examples.
Know that AI is tested after training.
Group examples by label.
Spot labelling mistakes.
Experience learning from examples.
Explain how AI learns.

guide.what: AI is trained with many labelled examples. More examples, and more different ones, help it learn well. Wrong or too few examples make it make mistakes.
steps: Play 'teach me': your child shows you 3 examples of a new thing.
Talk about why a voice helper does not understand some accents.
Sort photos into labelled albums.
home: Make labelled picture cards for a sorting game.
Find something AI got wrong and talk about why.
guide.watch: Mistakes are a good teaching moment: ask 'What examples was it missing?'

title: Using AI to learn Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on using ai to learn, from "AI as a Study Buddy" to "My Learning Plan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know good ways to learn with AI.
Write clear questions (prompts).
Check AI answers.
Know why our own work matters.
Write a good learning prompt.
Know that explaining in your own words shows learning.
Use AI to practise skills.
Use question words to ask AI.
Choose trusted sources.
Plan how to learn with AI.

guide.what: AI can be a study buddy: it can explain, give practice and quiz you. Ask clear questions, check answers in books or with teachers, and always do your own work.
steps: Ask AI together for 3 practice questions, then solve them on paper.
Compare a vague and a clear question.
Check an AI fact in a library book.
home: Make a 'good questions' list.
Let your child quiz you using AI questions they checked.
guide.watch: Watch for children letting AI think for them. Ask them to explain the answer in their own words.

Describe how AI recognises images.
Understand speech recognition and natural language.
Know that AI can make pictures and voices that look real.
Apply perception ideas to a design.
Understand that pictures are made of pixels.
Make a picture from pixels.
Sequence how a voice helper works.
Link machines and sensors.
Explain how AI senses the world.

guide.what: AI takes in the world through sensors: cameras to see and microphones to hear. It finds patterns in pictures and sounds, and can reply in words. AI can also make fake pictures and voices, so we check before we believe or share.
steps: Try voice typing together and look at the mistakes.
Talk about face unlock on phones.
Look at an obviously AI-made image and spot clues.
home: Make a list of sensors in your home.
Try a translator with simple Urdu sentences.
guide.watch: AI-made images are hard to spot even for adults. Teach the habit: pause, check the source, ask a grown-up.

title: Good prompts and checking answers Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on good prompts and checking answers, from "What Is a Prompt?" to "Prompt Challenge". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a prompt is the instruction we give AI.
Choose clear, detailed prompts.
Know that AI can invent facts.
Follow steps to check an AI answer.
Write detailed prompts.
Know what makes a prompt clear.
Spot weak prompts.
Ask follow-up questions to learn more.
Judge sources of information.
Write your own detailed prompts.

guide.what: A prompt is the question or instruction we give AI. Clear prompts with details get better answers. AI can sound sure but still be wrong or make things up, so we check facts in books, trusted websites or with teachers.
steps: Ask AI the same question two ways and compare.
Check one AI fact in an encyclopedia.
Praise detailed questions at home too.
home: Write a prompt for a bedtime story together.
Make a 'check it' checklist bookmark.
guide.watch: Children tend to believe confident writing. Make 'Where did it get that?' a family habit.

title: AI, fairness and being responsible Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on ai, fairness and being responsible, from "Fair for Everyone" to "Responsible Choices". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Understand that AI can be unfair if its data is unfair.
Spot unfair AI.
Protect personal information.
Know good uses of AI in society.
Make responsible choices with AI.
Keep accounts safe with strong passwords.
Behave kindly online.
Think about how AI changes work.
Apply fairness to a design.

guide.what: AI can be unfair if it learns from data that leaves people out. Responsible users protect their privacy, check answers, do their own work and think about how AI can help everyone.
steps: Talk about who might be left out by an app.
Make a family list of what is private.
Read news of AI helping farmers or doctors.
home: Design a fair AI for your school.
Write a thank-you note to someone who builds helpful technology.
guide.watch: Keep it hopeful: AI is a tool. People decide whether it is used fairly and kindly.

title: What is AI? Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on what is ai?, from "Smart Machines" to "What Did You Learn?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI is a computer program that can learn and help.
Spot everyday things that use AI.
Know that AI is not alive and has no feelings.
Link AI tools to their jobs.
Imagine how AI could help people.
Know that people design, build and test AI.
Compare what people and AI can do.
Spot AI in everyday places.
Learn simple AI vocabulary.
Review what AI is.

guide.what: AI (artificial intelligence) is a computer program made by people. It can learn from examples and help with jobs like answering questions or finding a road. AI is not alive and has no feelings.
steps: Point out AI around you: voice search, map directions, photo albums.
Ask: Is it alive? Who made it?
Talk about the difference between a toy robot and a real AI helper.
home: Ask a voice helper a question together and check the answer in a book.
Draw a robot that would help Dadi.
guide.watch: Children often think AI is a person inside the phone. Explain that it is a program that learned from lots of examples.

title: Machines learn from patterns Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on machines learn from patterns, from "What Is a Pattern?" to "Pattern Puzzle". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Find and continue patterns.
Sort new examples using a rule.
Explain how examples teach a rule.
Predict using a pattern.
Create a pattern.
Continue shape and colour patterns.
Find what breaks a pattern.
Sort using a rule.
Use patterns to make predictions.
Use patterns in word problems.

guide.what: AI learns by looking at many examples and finding patterns. Then it uses the pattern to make a guess. If the examples are wrong or too few, the guess can be wrong.
steps: Make bead or block patterns together.
Ask your child to teach you a rule using examples.
Play 'what comes next' in the car.
home: Find patterns on clothes, tiles and rugs.
Sort the laundry and say the rule you used.
guide.watch: Show that one example is not enough: if Robo only sees white cats, it may not know a black cat is a cat.

title: Asking AI safely Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on asking ai safely, from "Safe With a Grown-up" to "Safety Poster". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the safety rules for using AI.
Know what information to keep private.
Check AI answers with what you know.
Use kind and clear words, even with machines.
Remember AI safety rules.
Know who to ask for help online.
Ask helpful, kind questions.
Make healthy choices with screens.
Follow steps when using AI.
Share an AI safety rule.

guide.what: Children should use AI only with a grown-up. Keep personal details private, remember AI can be wrong, and always check answers with a trusted grown-up or book.
steps: Make a family rule: AI only with a grown-up.
Practise saying 'That is private' together.
Ask AI a simple question together and check the answer.
home: Make a safety poster for the fridge.
Role-play: a game asks your name. What do you say?
guide.watch: Children trust confident answers. Show them a wrong AI answer so they learn to check.

steps: Teach the sound first: "b" as in ball, then the name.
Show the capital and small letter side by side and trace both.
Sing the alphabet slowly while pointing to each letter.

Make letters with playdough or in a tray of flour.

home: Ask a voice helper a question together and check the answer in a book.

title: Our neighbourhood Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on our neighbourhood, from "What Is a Neighbourhood?" to "My Neighbourhood". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a neighbourhood is.
Name places in a neighbourhood and what they are for.
Know the people who help in a neighbourhood.
Choose the right helper for a problem.
Use north, south, east and west on a simple map.
Give directions on a map.
Know how to stay safe in the neighbourhood.
Know how to be a good neighbour.
Use maths to answer questions about a neighbourhood.
Describe your own neighbourhood.

guide.what: A neighbourhood is the area around our home: the places in it, the helpers who work there, reading a simple map and being a good neighbour.
steps: Go for a walk and name each place you pass.
Talk about who works in each place.
Draw a simple map of your street together.
home: Visit the local shop and let your child pay.
Make a thank-you card for a neighbourhood helper.
guide.watch: On a map, north is at the top. Children often mix up east and west, so practise with left and right first.

title: سردی کے الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on winter words (سردی کے الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read the big idea about winter.
Name winter clothes and things in Urdu.
Know the meanings of winter words.
Read a short passage and answer questions.
Sort things we use in winter and summer.
Use winter words in sentences.
Know opposites of weather words.
Read about snow in Pakistan.
Say one and two of winter things.
Write about your own winter.

guide.what: Winter words in Urdu: warm clothes, weather words like دھند and برف, a short passage about a winter morning, opposites, and writing about your own winter.
steps: Name each winter thing in Urdu as you get dressed.
Read the passage aloud and ask who, what and when.
Say each opposite pair together: سردی، گرمی.
home: Make a winter word wall with pictures.
Talk in Urdu about what the family eats in winter.
guide.watch: Some plurals change the ending (دستانہ، دستانے) and some stay the same (کمبل، کمبل). Point this out gently.

title: Sounds o, g, u, l Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Nursery English practice on sounds o, g, u, l, from "The Sound o" to "My l Picture". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hear the short o sound at the start of words.
Trace small o and capital O.
Hear and write the g sound.
Trace small g and capital G.
Hear and write the short u sound.
Trace small u and capital U.
Hear and write the l sound.
Trace small l and capital L.
Tell apart the sounds o, g, u and l.
Think of words that start with l.

guide.what: Four new letter sounds: o as in octopus, g as in goat, u as in umbrella and l as in lion. Children hear the sound, trace the letter and find words that start with it.
steps: Say the sound, not the letter name: /o/ not 'oh'.
Trace the letter in the air with a big arm first.
Play I spy with the four sounds.
home: Hunt for things at home that start with g or l.
Make the letters with play dough.
guide.watch: Small g and q look alike, and l and capital I look alike. Point out that g has a tail that curls to the left.
