obj: Know that 11 to 15 are ten and some more.
Count groups of 11 to 15.
Write the numbers 11, 12 and 13.
Write the numbers 14 and 15.
Say and write the numbers 1 to 15 in order.
Match a group to its number.
Compare groups up to 15.
Add a few more to ten.
Solve simple number stories to 15.
Draw a group of 13.

guide.what: Counting, reading and writing the numbers 11 to 15. Each one is ten and some more: thirteen is ten and three.
steps: Count out ten things first, then add the extra ones.
Say 'ten and two make twelve' as you count.
Point to each object once as you count.
home: Count 15 steps, peas or buttons together.
Find 11 to 15 on a calendar or clock.
guide.watch: Children often write 12 as 21. Show that the 1 (the ten) comes first.

title: My family Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on my family, from "This Is a Family" to "My Family". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the names of family members.
Name family members.
Tell young and old family members apart.
Know that people grow from babies to grandparents.
Show kindness to family.
Name things families do together.
Name feelings in the family.
Use polite words at home.
Count the people in a family.
Draw and name your own family.

guide.what: Who is in a family, names like Ammi, Abbu, Dada and Nani, how people grow up, and being kind at home.
steps: Look at family photos and name each person.
Talk about what each person does for the family.
Use the magic words yourself so your child copies you.
home: Make a family photo wall or a drawing of everyone.
Call a grandparent and let your child say hello.
guide.watch: Every family is different. Some children live with one parent or with grandparents. Talk about all families kindly.

title: نقطے والے حروف کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on letters with dots (نقطے والے حروف), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Trace letters with one dot.
Trace letters with two dots.
Trace letters with three dots.
Count the dots on a letter.
Say whether the dots are above or below.
Tell apart ب پ ت ث by their dots.
Hear the first letter in picture words.
Choose the letter that has a dot.
Spot letters that have dots.
Draw a picture for a dotted letter.

guide.what: Urdu letters that have dots: one dot (ب ن ج), two dots (ت ق ی) and three dots (پ ث چ), and whether the dots go above or below.
steps: Count the dots aloud with your child.
Show that ب پ ت ث have the same shape and only the dots change.
Add the dots last when writing a letter.
home: Make letters with a finger in flour and add dots with lentils.
Find dotted letters on a packet or a newspaper.
guide.watch: Children often put dots on the wrong side. Ask: does this dot go above or below?

title: Long vowel sounds with e Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of KG English practice on long vowel sounds with e, from "The Long e Sound" to "My Long e Sentence". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hear the difference between short e and long e.
Read and write ee words.
Read and write ea words.
Read short words where e says its name.
Sort long e words by spelling.
Use long e words in sentences.
Read a short text with long e words.
Hear rhymes with the long e sound.
Spot long e words in a sentence.
Write a sentence using a long e word.

guide.what: Long e says its own name. It is often spelt ee (bee, tree), ea (leaf, tea) or just e at the end of little words (me, we, she).
steps: Stretch the sound: beeeee.
Ask: short e like bed, or long e like bee?
Read ee and ea words on packets and signs.
home: Make an ee and ea word list on the fridge.
Play a rhyming game: bee, see, tree, me.
guide.watch: Both ee and ea make the same sound, so spelling takes practice. Focus on reading first.

title: Numbers to 50 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of KG Maths practice on numbers to 50, from "Tens and Ones" to "Write to 50". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that two-digit numbers are made of tens and ones.
Say and write numbers from 21 to 30.
Say and write numbers from 31 to 50.
Count in tens to 50.
Find numbers before, after and between.
Compare numbers up to 50.
Count groups of ten.
Solve number stories to 50.
Count on from any number to 50.
Write numbers from 1 to 50.

guide.what: Counting, reading and writing numbers to 50, counting in tens, and seeing that each number is tens and ones.
steps: Bundle straws or sticks in tens with a rubber band.
Count the tens first, then the ones.
Say numbers aloud as you count: thirty-one, thirty-two.
home: Count 50 grains of rice or 50 steps together.
Find numbers to 50 on a calendar, a ruler or a book.
guide.watch: Some children say 'thirty-ten' after 39. Practise the jump from 39 to 40 and 49 to 50.

title: Our solar system Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on our solar system, from "The Sun and Its Planets" to "My Space Picture". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that planets go around the Sun.
Know one fact about some planets.
Say the eight planets in order.
Know that Earth spins to make day and night.
Know some facts about the Moon.
Know facts about the Sun.
Know what astronauts need in space.
Sort things we see in the sky.
Use numbers to answer space questions.
Draw and label the solar system.

guide.what: The Sun is a star with eight planets going around it. We live on Earth. Earth spins to give us day and night, and the Moon goes around the Earth.
steps: Use a ball and a torch to show day and night.
Sing or say the planets in order.
Look at the Moon each night for a week.
home: Draw the Moon's shape each night and see it change.
Make a planet mobile from paper circles.
guide.watch: Never let children look straight at the Sun, even with sunglasses.

title: چار حرفی الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of KG Urdu practice on four letter words (چار حرفی الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Join four letters to make a word.
Read and write four letter words for pictures.
Break four letter words into letters.
Count three and four letter words.
Complete four letter words.
Know the meaning of four letter words.
Use four letter words in sentences.
Sort four letter words into animals and things.
Solve simple Urdu number stories.
Trace four letter words.

guide.what: Reading, joining and breaking four letter Urdu words like کتاب، بکری، چاند and مرغی, and using them in short sentences.
steps: Say each letter, then blend them into the word.
Clap once for each letter.
Point out that some letters, like ا and د, do not join to the next letter.
home: Label things at home with four letter words: کرسی، کتاب، چابی.
Read short words on packets together.
guide.watch: The letter ھ counts as a letter, so گھر has three letters. Check this when counting.

title: Typing my name Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 ICT practice on typing my name, from "The Keyboard" to "My Name". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a keyboard is for.
Know the special keys on a keyboard.
Know that keyboard letters are not in ABC order.
Choose the right key for a job.
Follow the steps to type a name.
Tell capital and small letters apart.
Know how to sit and type safely.
Use Backspace to fix typing mistakes.
Count letters in a name.
Plan how to type your own name.

guide.what: Using a keyboard to type: letter rows, special keys such as Shift, Space bar, Backspace and Enter, and typing your own name with a capital letter.
steps: Let your child find each letter of their name on a keyboard.
Show how Shift makes a capital letter.
Practise fixing a mistake with Backspace.
home: Type a family member's name in a notes app.
Play a find-the-letter race on the keyboard.
guide.watch: Children may hold Caps Lock on for everything. Teach Shift for one capital letter at the start of a name.

title: Adverbs Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 English practice on adverbs, from "What Is an Adverb?" to "My Adverb Sentences". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that an adverb tells us more about a verb.
Make adverbs by adding -ly.
Use the y to i spelling rule for adverbs.
Use adverbs that tell when.
Sort adverbs by the question they answer.
Use adverbs that tell how often.
Choose adverbs that match an action.
Pick adverbs that make sense.
Find adverbs in a short text.
Write sentences with adverbs.

guide.what: Adverbs tell us more about a verb: how (slowly), when (tomorrow), where (outside) and how often (always). Many end in -ly.
steps: Find the verb first, then ask: how? when? where? how often?
Practise adding -ly and the y to i rule.
Read a story page and hunt for adverbs together.
home: Play an adverb game: one person acts, for example walking sleepily, and the others guess the adverb.
Give an order such as clap your hands, then add an adverb: loudly, softly, quickly.
guide.watch: Not every adverb ends in -ly (fast, well, soon), and not every -ly word is an adverb (friendly, lovely are describing words).

title: Place value to 1000 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on place value to 1000, from "Hundreds, Tens and Ones" to "Number Puzzles". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the value of each digit in a 3-digit number.
Make a 3-digit number from hundreds, tens and ones.
Write numbers in expanded form.
Find the value of a digit by its place.
Compare 3-digit numbers using place value.
Order 3-digit numbers.
Add and take away 10 and 100.
Use hundreds, tens and ones with money.
Count on and back in 10s and 100s.
Use place value to solve puzzles.

guide.what: Numbers up to 1000: hundreds, tens and ones, expanded form, comparing and ordering, 10 and 100 more or less, and using rupee notes as a model.
steps: Use Rs 100, Rs 10 and Rs 1 play money to build numbers.
Say each number in parts: 472 is 400 and 70 and 2.
Compare numbers by looking at the hundreds first.
home: Read prices at the shop and say how many hundreds and tens they have.
Roll three dice and make the biggest and smallest number.
guide.watch: Zero matters: 507 has no tens. Children often write 5007 or 57. Use a place value chart with H, T and O columns.

title: Our senses Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on our senses, from "Our Five Senses" to "My Senses". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the five senses.
Match each sense to its body part.
Choose the sense we use for different things.
Know that foods can be sweet, sour or salty.
Describe things we touch.
Know how our senses warn us of danger.
Know that animals have strong senses.
Plan a simple test using the sense of touch.
Use maths to answer questions about senses.
Describe how you use your senses.

guide.what: The five senses (sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch), the body parts we use for each, tastes, how senses keep us safe and how some animals have very strong senses.
steps: Name each sense and point to the body part.
Close your eyes and use only one sense to guess things.
Talk about how a sense warns us of danger.
home: Make a mystery bag with a few things to feel and guess.
Do a taste test with sugar, lemon and salt on a spoon.
guide.watch: Spicy is a feeling of heat, not one of the main tastes. Children may also forget that touch uses the whole skin, not just the hands.

title: The Harappan city Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 History practice on the harappan city, from "A City by the River" to "A Day in Harappa". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know where and when Harappa was built.
Describe how Harappan people built their city.
Know that Harappa had a drain system.
Know what Harappan seals were.
Know the jobs and things of Harappan life.
Compare Harappan life with life today.
Know how Harappa was discovered.
Use maths with Harappan facts.
Recall facts about Harappa.
Write about life in an ancient city.

guide.what: Harappa, a great Indus Valley city built about 4500 years ago by the Ravi River in Punjab: baked bricks, straight streets, covered drains, seals, farming and trade.
steps: Find Harappa near Sahiwal on a map of Pakistan.
Talk about how the city stayed clean without modern pipes.
Compare Harappan things with what we use today.
home: Make a seal from clay or dough and press an animal picture into it.
Visit the Lahore Museum or look at photos of Harappan seals.
guide.watch: Children may think Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are the same city. They are two cities of the same Indus Valley people, far apart.

title: Weather maps Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on weather maps, from "What Is Weather?" to "My Weather Diary". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what weather is.
Read weather symbols.
Read a simple weather map with directions.
Find places and weather on a map.
Read temperatures in degrees Celsius.
Find the difference between temperatures.
Choose clothes for the weather.
Use a weather forecast to plan.
Know the weather in different parts of Pakistan.
Record the weather.

guide.what: Weather, weather symbols, reading a simple weather map of Pakistan with compass directions, temperature in degrees Celsius and using a forecast.
steps: Watch the weather report on TV and spot the symbols.
Look at a thermometer or weather app together.
Talk about which places in Pakistan are hot or cold today.
home: Keep a weather diary for a week with a symbol for each day.
Make a weather map of your city with paper symbols.
guide.watch: On a map, north is at the top, so cities like Gilgit are at the top. Children may think up on a map means up in the sky.

title: Our local government Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on our local government, from "Who Looks After Our Town?" to "If I Were Mayor". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what local government is.
Name services the local government gives.
Know who leads the local government.
Know the steps of a simple election.
Know which problems the local government solves.
Know that taxes pay for services.
Know how citizens can help the local government.
Understand how a council makes choices.
Write to a local leader about a problem.
Share ideas for making a town better.

guide.what: Local government: the services it gives (water, rubbish, roads, lights, parks), how we choose councillors and a mayor by voting, taxes, and how citizens can help.
steps: Spot local services on a walk: bins, street lights, parks.
Talk about who to tell when a street light is broken.
Explain voting with a family vote, for example on a dinner choice.
home: Hold a family election with paper votes in a box.
Write a short thank-you note to the people who collect rubbish.
guide.watch: Children may think the Prime Minister fixes every street. Explain that local problems go to local leaders first.

title: فعل کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on verbs (فعل), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know that a verb is a doing word.
Write the verb that matches the picture.
Tell nouns and verbs apart.
Match animals to what they do.
Know verbs with opposite meanings.
Match the verb to a boy or a girl.
Use verbs to give instructions in order.
Read Urdu number stories with verbs.
Find verbs in a short story.
Write sentences with verbs.

guide.what: Verbs (فعل) in Urdu: doing words like دوڑنا، لکھنا، کھیلنا. Children find verbs, tell nouns and verbs apart, learn opposite verbs and match verbs to a boy, a girl or many children.
steps: Act out a verb and let your child say it in Urdu.
Ask: what is he or she doing? to find the verb.
Practise کھیلتا، کھیلتی، کھیلتے with family members.
home: Play Simon says in Urdu: بیٹھو، اٹھو، تالی بجاؤ.
Read a short Urdu story and underline the verbs.
guide.watch: Some words are both a noun and a verb, like کھانا (food, to eat). Look at the sentence to decide.

title: Typing practice Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 ICT practice on typing practice, from "The Home Row" to "Practice Sheet". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the home row keys.
Know which finger goes on each home key.
Spell words with home row letters.
Know the top, home and bottom rows.
Use special keys when typing.
Check typing for capitals and full stops.
Use maths to talk about typing speed.
Know how to sit and type safely.
Follow steps to get better at typing.
Practise typing words and sentences.

guide.what: Typing with the right fingers: the home row (A S D F, J K L), the bumps on F and J, top and bottom rows, handy keys such as Space bar, Shift, Enter and Backspace, and sitting well.
steps: Show the bumps on F and J and let your child find them with eyes closed.
Practise short home row words: sad, dad, ask.
Keep sessions to 10 or 15 minutes.
home: Use a free typing game together for a few minutes a day.
Type a short shopping list with capital letters and full stops.
guide.watch: Children often look down at their hands. Cover the hands with a light cloth for a minute so they learn to feel the keys.

title: Adverbs and adverbials Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 English practice on adverbs and adverbials, from "Adverbs Add Detail" to "Write with Adverbials". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that adverbs tell us how, when, where and how often.
Group adverbs by the question they answer.
Know that a group of words can work like an adverb.
Use a comma after a fronted adverbial.
Move adverbials to vary sentences.
Use adverbs that show how much.
Use more, most, -er and -est with adverbs.
Choose precise adverbs for actions.
Find adverbials in a text.
Use adverbs and fronted adverbials in writing.

guide.what: Adverbs and adverbials at Grade 4 level: adverbs of how, when, where and how often, adverbs of degree (very, quite, too), adverbial phrases, fronted adverbials with a comma, and comparing adverbs (faster, more carefully, better).
steps: Ask how? when? where? how often? about each verb in a sentence.
Point out fronted adverbials in story books and look for the comma.
Practise moving an adverbial from the end of a sentence to the front.
home: Play adverb charades: act out a task in the manner of an adverb (sleepily, angrily) while others guess.
Write a recipe together and start each step with an adverbial: First, After two minutes, Finally.
guide.watch: Children often forget the comma after a fronted adverbial, or think every -ly word is an adverb. Friendly and lovely are adjectives.

title: Multiplying 2-digit numbers Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on multiplying 2-digit numbers, from "Multiplying by 10" to "Number Detective". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Multiply numbers by 10 and 100.
Multiply by multiples of 10.
Multiply a 2-digit number by a 1-digit number by partitioning.
Use the grid method to multiply.
Use the short column method.
Multiply a 2-digit number by a 2-digit number.
Use multiplication in real life.
Solve one-step and two-step word problems.
Estimate to check answers.
Reason about multiplication.

guide.what: Multiplying 2-digit numbers: times 10 and 100, multiples of 10, partitioning, the grid method, the short column method, a first look at 2-digit × 2-digit using a grid, estimating and word problems.
steps: Make sure times tables to 10 × 10 are quick before starting.
Say the parts out loud: 23 × 4 is 20 fours and 3 fours.
Estimate first, then check if the answer is sensible.
home: At the shop, work out the cost of several of the same item, for example 3 packets at Rs 45.
Count eggs in trays or chairs in rows and multiply.
guide.watch: Children often forget to add the carried ten in the column method, or multiply only the ones digit. The grid method helps them see both parts.

title: Food chains Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on food chains, from "Energy from the Sun" to "My Food Chain". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that food chains start with the Sun and plants.
Tell producers and consumers apart.
Read a food chain with arrows.
Group animals by what they eat.
Know what predators and prey are.
Order living things in a food chain.
Know what decomposers do.
Predict what happens when a food chain changes.
Use maths with food chain facts.
Make and explain a food chain.

guide.what: Food chains: plants are producers that make food from sunlight, animals are consumers. Arrows show energy moving. Herbivores, carnivores and omnivores, predators and prey, decomposers, and what happens when a chain changes.
steps: Check that arrows point from the food to the eater.
Ask what your child ate for lunch and trace it back to a plant.
Talk about animals that are both predators and prey.
home: Look under a stone or a pile of leaves for decomposers like worms.
Make a paper chain with one living thing on each link.
guide.watch: Children often draw the arrow the wrong way, from the eater to the food. The arrow means is eaten by and shows where the energy goes.

title: The Mughal empire Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 History practice on the mughal empire, from "Who Were the Mughals?" to "Be a Historian". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know when the Mughal empire began.
Name the first six Mughal emperors in order.
Know why Akbar is remembered.
Know famous Mughal buildings in Pakistan.
Describe a Mughal garden.
Know the arts of the Mughal period.
Know about life at the Mughal court.
Use dates to work out time.
Know how the Mughal empire ended.
Explain why the Mughals are important.

guide.what: The Mughal empire (1526 to 1857): Babur and the first six emperors, Akbar, Mughal buildings in Lahore such as the Badshahi Mosque, Shalimar Gardens and Lahore Fort, gardens, miniature painting, Persian at court and the end of the empire.
steps: Find Lahore, Agra and Delhi on a map.
Look at photos of the Badshahi Mosque and Shalimar Gardens together.
Make a family timeline and compare it with the Mughal timeline.
home: Visit the Lahore Fort, Badshahi Mosque or Shalimar Gardens, or watch a short video tour.
Try drawing a small miniature painting with fine pencils and bright colours.
guide.watch: Children may think the Taj Mahal is in Pakistan. It is in Agra, India. The Mughal buildings in Pakistan include the Badshahi Mosque, Lahore Fort and Shalimar Gardens.

title: Climate zones of the world Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on climate zones of the world, from "Weather and Climate" to "My Climate Fact File". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell the difference between weather and climate.
Know why it is hotter near the Equator.
Name the main climate zones.
Describe the tropical climate.
Describe the desert climate.
Describe the polar climate.
Know that Pakistan has more than one climate.
Know how climate affects homes, clothes and food.
Read temperature data and compare places.
Present facts about a climate zone.

guide.what: Climate zones of the world: weather and climate, the Equator and the poles, tropical, desert, temperate, polar and mountain climates, the many climates of Pakistan, and how climate shapes homes, clothes and food.
steps: Find the Equator and the poles on a globe or atlas.
Compare today's weather in Karachi, Lahore and Skardu on a weather app.
Talk about what you pack for a trip to Murree compared to Karachi.
home: Make a climate zone poster with pictures cut from magazines.
Fill a jar with sand and one with soil, water them, and see which dries first.
guide.watch: Children often mix up weather and climate. Weather changes day to day; climate is the usual pattern over many years.

title: Provinces and their capitals Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on provinces and their capitals, from "Pakistan's Provinces" to "My Province". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that Pakistan has four provinces.
Name provincial capitals.
Use a map to locate provinces.
Know key facts about Punjab.
Know key facts about Sindh.
Know key facts about Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Know key facts about Balochistan.
Recall facts about each province.
Use distances and times between cities.
Describe your own province.

guide.what: Provinces and capitals of Pakistan: Punjab (Lahore), Sindh (Karachi), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Peshawar), Balochistan (Quetta), plus Islamabad Capital Territory, Gilgit-Baltistan (Gilgit) and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (Muzaffarabad). Facts about land, people, crops and famous places, with map and travel problems.
steps: Use a map of Pakistan to point to each province and its capital.
Talk about relatives or friends who live in other provinces.
Make flash cards with a province on one side and its capital on the other.
home: Cook or taste a dish from each province over a month.
Plan an imaginary road trip that visits all four provincial capitals.
guide.watch: Children sometimes think Karachi is the capital of Pakistan. It was the first capital, but Islamabad has been the capital since the 1960s. Karachi is the capital of Sindh.

title: زمانہ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on tenses (زمانہ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know the three tenses in Urdu.
Write verbs in the past tense.
Use the present tense.
Change sentences into the future tense.
Write one verb in all three tenses.
Sort time words by tense.
Use tense with pictures.
Read Urdu number stories with tenses.
Find tenses in a story.
Write about yourself in three tenses.

guide.what: Tenses (زمانہ) in Urdu: past (ماضی), present (حال) and future (مستقبل). Children spot the tense of a sentence, change verbs from one tense to another, use time words such as کل، آج، اگلے سال and find tenses in a story.
steps: Ask three questions in Urdu: کل کیا کیا؟ ابھی کیا کر رہے ہو؟ کل کیا کرو گے؟
Point out گا، گی، گے at the end of future sentences.
Read an Urdu story and ask which tense it is told in.
home: Keep a three-line Urdu diary for a week: one line past, one present, one future.
Play a tense game: say a verb and ask your child to use it in all three tenses.
guide.watch: کل can mean yesterday or tomorrow in Urdu. The verb shows which one: کل گیا (yesterday), کل جاؤں گا (tomorrow).

title: Spreadsheets: totals Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 ICT practice on spreadsheets: totals, from "Cells, Rows and Columns" to "My Spending Sheet". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the parts of a spreadsheet.
Find cells by their address.
Know that a formula does a sum for us.
Use SUM to add a range of cells.
Use totals to understand data.
Spot and fix formula mistakes.
Know useful spreadsheet tools.
Total survey data in a spreadsheet.
Follow steps to build a spreadsheet with totals.
Plan a spreadsheet with a total.

guide.what: Spreadsheets with totals: cells, rows, columns and cell addresses (B3), formulas that start with =, the +, -, * and / signs, the SUM function with ranges (B2:B5), AutoSum and the fill handle, and using totals to answer questions.
steps: Open a free spreadsheet app and type a family shopping list together.
Change a number and watch the total update by itself.
Say cell addresses aloud: column letter first, then row number.
home: Keep a spreadsheet of pocket money or reading minutes for a month.
Make a chart from a class or family survey.
guide.watch: Children often forget the = sign, so the formula shows as text. They may also mix up rows (numbers, across) and columns (letters, down).

title: Smart helpers at home Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on smart helpers at home, from "Smart Helpers" to "My Dream Helper". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a smart helper is.
Spot machines that have AI inside.
Link smart helpers to the jobs they do.
Name everyday smart machines.
Follow the steps to ask a smart speaker.
Solve word problems about smart helpers.
Know what machines can do and what people do best.
Make safe rules for smart helpers.
Learn the parts of a smart helper.
Imagine a helpful machine.

guide.what: Smart helpers are machines with AI inside, like smart speakers, phone alarms, map apps and smart TVs. They listen or look, then help with small jobs. They are not people and cannot care for us the way family does.
steps: Point out smart helpers in your home and say what each one does.
Ask your child: is it a machine or a person?
Make two family rules for using smart helpers.
home: Set a kitchen timer together and count down.
Draw the smart helpers in your house on one page.
guide.watch: Young children often think the speaker is a little person. Say clearly: it is a machine that people made.

words: plays a song when you ask
wakes you up in the morning
shows the way to Nano's house

title: Robots around us Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on robots around us, from "What Is a Robot?" to "Design a Robot". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a robot senses, thinks and moves.
Tell robots apart from other things.
Know the jobs robots do.
Know the three steps a robot follows.
Know the parts that help a robot work.
Know which jobs suit robots and which need people.
Solve word problems about robots.
Know what robots can and cannot do.
Know that people build, charge and fix robots.
Design a robot for a job.

guide.what: A robot is a machine that senses, thinks and acts to do a job. Robots work in factories, farms, hospitals, homes and even on Mars. People build them, charge them and fix them. Robots are not alive.
steps: Spot robots in cartoons and real life and ask: what is its job?
Play 'sense, think, act': you are the robot, your child gives the steps.
Talk about jobs a robot could never do, like giving a hug.
home: Build a robot from old boxes and give it a job.
Watch a short video of a farm or factory robot together.
guide.watch: Cartoon robots talk and feel. Explain that real robots only follow instructions and patterns they learned.

title: Sorting like a computer Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on sorting like a computer, from "What Is Sorting?" to "My Sorting Rule". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that sorting means putting things into groups by a rule.
Sort pictures into two groups.
Sort things by colour.
Sort animals by the number of legs.
Sort using a yes or no question.
Sort things by season.
Find the thing that breaks the rule.
Follow the steps a computer uses to sort.
Solve sorting word problems.
Make up a sorting rule.

guide.what: Sorting means putting things into groups by a rule, such as colour, shape, size or number of legs. Computers sort by asking simple yes or no questions very fast. AI uses sorting to group photos, songs and messages.
steps: Sort laundry, cutlery or toys together and say the rule out loud.
Ask yes or no sorting questions: is it round? is it red?
Look at how a phone groups photos of the same person.
home: Play 'guess my rule': sort a few things and let your child guess the rule.
Sort fruit in the kitchen by colour.
guide.watch: Some things fit two groups. Praise your child for noticing and talk about choosing one clear rule.

title: Good questions Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on good questions, from "What Is a Good Question?" to "My Questions". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a good question is clear and kind.
Use question words to start questions.
Tell clear questions from unclear ones.
Choose the clearer question.
Ask questions about the world.
Ask questions with good manners.
Follow the steps of asking a good question.
Tell questions from telling sentences.
Solve word problems about questions.
Write your own clear questions.

guide.what: A good question is clear and kind and says exactly what you want to know. Question words like who, what, where, when, why and how help us start. AI helpers, like people, give better answers to clear questions, and we still check the answer.
steps: Play 'question of the day' at dinner.
When your child asks 'that?', help them say a full, clear question.
Model kind words: please and thank you, even to a speaker.
home: Make a question word fan with who, what, where, when, why and how.
Write three questions about animals and find the answers in a book.
guide.watch: Do not worry if questions are messy at first. Help your child add one detail: 'What do you want to know about camels?'

title: Real or pretend? Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on real or pretend?, from "Real or Pretend?" to "Draw Real and Pretend". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the difference between real and pretend.
Sort real and pretend creatures.
Decide if something could really happen.
Know that AI can make pictures that look real.
Look for clues in pictures.
Follow steps before believing a picture.
Sort facts and pretend sentences.
Solve word problems about real and pretend things.
Describe pretend creatures.
Show real and pretend in pictures.

guide.what: Real things exist in our world; pretend things come from stories and imagination. Pretend is fun in stories and play. AI can now make pretend pictures and videos that look real, so children learn to stop, think, ask a grown-up and check.
steps: Read a story and ask: which parts are real, which are pretend?
Look at a silly picture together and find the clues.
Praise your child for saying 'I am not sure, let me check'.
home: Draw a pretend animal and give it a name.
Make a 'real or pretend?' card game with pictures from magazines.
guide.watch: Keep imagination joyful. The aim is not to stop pretend play, but to know when something says it is real and is not.

title: Voices and speakers Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on voices and speakers, from "Machines That Hear and Talk" to "My Talking Machine". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know how a machine hears and talks.
Know which parts hear and which talk.
Know the steps a voice helper follows.
Know how to speak so a machine understands.
Tell loud and quiet sounds apart.
Solve word problems about volume.
Know that voice helpers can make mistakes.
Know everyday machines that talk.
Use voice helpers politely and safely.
Design a talking machine.

guide.what: Voice helpers hear us with a microphone, turn our sounds into words with AI, find an answer and talk back through a speaker. They can mishear words, so we speak clearly, check answers and use good manners.
steps: Try voice typing together and look for funny mistakes.
Talk about machines that speak: lifts, maps, toys.
Practise speaking clearly and slowly.
home: Record your child's voice and play it back.
Make a list of all the things at home that make sounds.
guide.watch: Some voice helpers find children's voices harder to understand. Reassure your child that it is the machine, not them.

title: Kind and fair Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on kind and fair, from "Kind and Fair" to "My Kindness Promise". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what kind and fair mean.
Spot kind and unkind actions.
Share things fairly.
Know that AI must learn from everyone to be fair.
Know that AI should work for all kinds of people.
Tell kind and unkind words apart.
Follow the steps of taking turns.
Judge if a machine or game is fair.
Choose kind actions.
Make a promise to be kind and fair.

pages.title: A Robot That Was Not Fair

guide.what: Fair means everyone gets a turn and a chance; kind means caring how others feel. AI should be fair too: it must learn from all kinds of people, young and old, so it works for everyone. Children practise fairness by sharing, taking turns and using kind words online and off.
steps: Use a timer to share the tablet fairly.
Talk about who might be left out in a game or an app.
Praise kind words when you hear them.
home: Make a family kindness jar and add a note for each kind act.
Share a snack fairly and count the pieces.
guide.watch: Children have a strong sense of fairness. Use it: 'Would that be fair for everyone?'

title: Pictures and patterns Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on pictures and patterns, from "How AI Knows Pictures" to "My Picture Pattern". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI finds patterns in pictures.
Name the clues that help us know an animal.
Use clues to name an animal.
Continue picture patterns.
Find shapes in everyday things.
Know that AI needs many different pictures.
Solve word problems about photos.
Know patterns on animals.
Sort pictures by a clue.
Make your own picture pattern.

guide.what: AI recognises pictures by finding patterns: shapes, colours, lines and clues like whiskers or stripes. It needs to see many different pictures to learn well. Children practise the same skill by spotting clues, shapes and repeating patterns.
steps: Play 'I spy a shape' around the house.
Describe an animal by its clues and let your child guess.
Look at patterns on clothes, tiles and rugs.
home: Make a pattern with spoons and forks on the table.
Draw an animal and label its clues.
guide.watch: If your child only knows one kind of something (only yellow mangoes), show them more. That is exactly how AI learns too.

title: Sorting and labelling Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on sorting and labelling, from "Sort, Then Label" to "My Sorting Project". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI sorts data into groups and gives each group a label.
Label pictures with the right word.
Sort pictures by a science rule.
Sort using two clues together.
Spot labelling mistakes that confuse AI.
Explain what happens when labels are wrong.
Follow the steps an app uses to sort photos.
Solve word problems about sorting data.
Know that labels help people and machines find things.
Plan and label your own sorting.

guide.what: Sorting puts data into groups by a rule, and labels are the name tags for those groups. AI learns from sorted, labelled data, often labelled by people. Wrong labels teach AI the wrong thing, so labels must be checked.
steps: Label jars or boxes at home together.
Ask: what rule did you use to sort these?
Look at how a phone groups photos into albums.
home: Sort a pile of socks or books and make paper labels.
Make a 'wrong label' game: label a cup 'shoe' and talk about the confusion.
guide.watch: Some things fit two groups. Ask your child to choose one clear rule and explain it.

title: Predictions Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on predictions, from "What Is a Prediction?" to "My Prediction Diary". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a prediction is a guess about what will happen, based on data.
Predict using number and picture patterns.
Use clues to predict the weather.
Predict from a table of data.
Tell predictions based on data from wild guesses.
Know the steps AI uses to make a prediction.
Know everyday AI predictions.
Solve word problems using patterns.
Know why predictions can be wrong.
Make and test your own predictions.

guide.what: A prediction is a careful guess about what will happen, based on patterns in past data. AI predicts the weather, traffic and the next word we type. Predictions can be wrong, so people check them, and more good data can make them better.
steps: Predict the weather together each morning and check in the evening.
Ask: what clues did you use to guess?
Look at the 'next word' suggestions when typing a message.
home: Keep a family prediction chart for a week.
Predict how many minutes the school drive will take, then time it.
guide.watch: Praise good reasoning even when the prediction turns out wrong. The thinking matters more than being right.

title: Robots and sensors Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on robots and sensors, from "Robots Sense the World" to "Design a Sensor Robot". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that sensors help robots take in information.
Match human senses to robot sensors.
Choose the right sensor for a job.
Know how a robot turns sensing into action.
Follow sensor rules like a robot.
Spot sensors in everyday things.
Solve word problems about robots and sensors.
Know that sensors can make mistakes.
Know how robot sensors help in real life.
Plan which sensors a robot needs.

guide.what: Sensors let machines notice the world: cameras sense light, microphones sense sound, and touch, heat and motion sensors feel pushes, warmth and movement. A robot senses, thinks and acts, again and again. Sensors can be confused by dust, noise or bright light.
steps: Find sensors at home: lights, doors, phones, remotes.
Play 'robot rules': you give an if-then rule, your child acts it out.
Compare our five senses with robot sensors.
home: Build a cardboard robot and label its sensors.
Walk past an automatic door and talk about how it knew you were there.
guide.watch: If-then rules (if wall, then turn) are the first step in coding. Keep them simple and fun.

title: Asking clear questions Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on asking clear questions, from "Clear Questions Get Clear Answers" to "Write Your Own Prompts". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a clear question gives the details you need.
Know what to put in a clear question.
Choose clear, detailed questions.
Add details to questions about pictures.
Improve a question with one detail.
Follow the steps for writing a clear question.
Tell polite, clear questions from rude or unclear ones.
Solve word problems about asking questions.
Ask follow-up questions to learn more.
Write your own clear prompts.

guide.what: A prompt is the question we ask an AI. Clear prompts say what we want, the topic, how much and who it is for. Polite, detailed questions and good follow-ups get better answers from people and from AI.
steps: Turn your child's short questions into full ones together.
Play 'add a detail': take a plain question and make it clearer.
Ask follow-ups at dinner: tell me more, why, give me an example.
home: Write a question card for each family member to answer.
Ask a voice helper a vague question and a clear one and compare.
guide.watch: Children love being 'question detectives'. Praise a detail they add, not only the right answer.

title: Checking answers Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on checking answers, from "Stop and Check" to "My Checking Badge". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that we check AI answers before we trust them.
Use what you know to check answers.
Check maths answers by working them out.
Choose a good source for each question.
Judge where information comes from.
Follow steps to check an answer.
Find facts that do not make sense.
Solve word problems about checking answers.
Know which answers need checking.
Practise checking facts.

guide.what: AI can sound sure and still be wrong, or even make things up. Smart learners stop and check: work it out, look in a book, atlas or dictionary, or ask a teacher or parent. Ideas and stories are fine as they are, but facts need checking.
steps: Check one fact a day together in a book or atlas.
Ask: how do we know that is true?
Share a time you were wrong and how you found out.
home: Make a 'stop and check' bookmark.
Play 'true or made up' with silly and real facts.
guide.watch: Children believe confident answers. Showing them an AI mistake is one of the best lessons you can give.

title: Pictures made by AI Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on pictures made by ai, from "AI Can Make Pictures" to "Your Own Picture". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI can make new pictures from words.
Tell possible pictures from made-up ones.
Know clues that a picture may be made by AI.
Use describing words in picture prompts.
Understand how AI pictures are made.
Follow steps before sharing a picture.
Know kind and unkind uses of AI pictures.
Solve word problems about AI pictures.
Know that people are creative in their own way.
Compare your own drawing with a picture prompt.

pages.title: Made by a Person or AI?

guide.what: Some AI makes new pictures from words. It learned from millions of pictures made by people. AI pictures can look real even when they show things that never happened, so we look for clues, ask a grown-up and only share what is true and kind.
steps: Look at a picture together and ask: could this be real?
Spot clues: extra fingers, squiggly writing, odd shadows.
Talk about why we never make fake pictures of real people.
home: Draw a silly picture and write the prompt an AI might need.
Visit truck art or local art and talk about human artists.
guide.watch: Even adults are fooled by AI pictures. Make 'stop, look, ask' a family habit.

title: Privacy and safety Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on privacy and safety, from "Keep It Private" to "My Safety Shield". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what personal information is and why we keep it private.
Sort information into private and OK to share.
Know what makes a strong password.
Choose safe actions online.
Follow steps when something online feels wrong.
Know trusted grown-ups who can help.
Know that photos are personal information.
Solve word problems about online safety.
Sort personal and general information.
Write your own online safety rules.

guide.what: Personal information like our full name, address, school, phone number, passwords and photos stays private. Apps and AI do not need it to help us. Strong passwords are long and mixed. If anything online feels wrong, stop, close it and tell a trusted grown-up.
steps: Make a family list of what is private.
Practise saying 'That is private, I will ask a grown-up'.
Make a strong password together using silly words and numbers.
home: Draw a safety shield for the fridge.
Role-play: a game asks for your address. What do you do?
guide.watch: Children may not see a school name or a photo as personal. Explain that it helps strangers find them.

title: AI in the doctor's clinic Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on ai in the doctor's clinic, from "AI Helps Doctors" to "Design a Clinic Helper". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI can help doctors, but doctors decide.
Name tools found in a clinic.
Know what doctors do and how AI helps.
Sequence a visit to the doctor.
Know how AI learns to read X-rays.
Solve word problems set in a clinic.
Know that health information must be kept private.
Know habits that keep us well.
Know the people and machines in a clinic.
Plan a helpful, safe AI for a clinic.

guide.what: In clinics, AI can help doctors look at X-rays quickly, send reminders and keep records tidy. It learned from pictures labelled by doctors. But doctors and nurses check, decide and care for patients, and health records are always private.
steps: Talk about what happens at a check-up before the next visit.
Ask: what does the doctor do that a machine cannot?
Practise healthy habits: handwashing, brushing, sleep.
home: Play 'clinic' with a toy stethoscope and a helper robot.
Draw the people who work in a clinic and their jobs.
guide.watch: If your child is nervous about doctors, keep the focus on helpers who care. The machine only helps the doctor.

title: How chatbots work Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on how chatbots work, from "What Is a Chatbot?" to "My Chatbot Questions". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a chatbot predicts words from patterns it learned.
Predict words from patterns, the way a chatbot does.
Compare what chatbots and people can do.
Sequence what happens in a chatbot conversation.
Learn the key words about chatbots.
Correct common ideas about chatbots.
Solve word problems about chatbots.
Find and fix a chatbot mistake.
Use chatbots safely and wisely.
Plan clear, safe questions for a chatbot.

guide.what: A chatbot is an AI that learned from a huge amount of text. When we ask it something, it predicts the most likely next words, one after another. That is why it can sound clever and sure, but still make up facts. It is a tool, not a person, so we keep private things private and check what it says.
steps: Play 'guess the next word' at dinner to show how prediction works.
Ask: who wrote the text the chatbot learned from?
Make 'check it in a book' a family habit.
home: Write a short chat between a child and a chatbot where the chatbot makes a mistake, then fix it.
Make a bookmark: Ask clearly, keep private, check it.
guide.watch: Children may think a chatbot 'knows' or 'understands' like a person. Use the words 'predicts' and 'guesses' to keep it real.

title: Data and bias Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on data and bias, from "What Is Data?" to "My Fair Survey". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what data is and why it matters for AI.
Name different kinds of data.
See how missing data causes mistakes.
Spot data that leaves people out.
Collect and read data in a tally.
Find the bias in a data set.
Learn key words about data.
Plan how to reduce bias.
Use numbers to think about data.
Design a fair way to collect data.

guide.what: Data is information like numbers, words, pictures and sounds. AI learns from data. When the data leaves some people or things out, the AI learns a lopsided picture, which we call bias. We can make AI fairer by checking who is missing, adding more examples and testing it with everyone.
steps: Do a family survey (favourite food, favourite colour) and make a tally.
Ask: who might be left out of this app?
Look at a bar chart in a newspaper together.
home: Run a small survey with cousins and draw a pictograph.
Find an app or game and talk about who it might not work well for.
guide.watch: Bias can be a big word. Keep it simple: the AI only knows what it has seen, so we make sure it sees everyone.

title: Image recognition Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on image recognition, from "How AI Sees Pictures" to "Be the Image AI". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI recognises pictures by learning features from labelled examples.
Name features that help us recognise things.
Sequence how image recognition is trained.
Link image recognition to real uses.
Know what makes pictures hard to recognise.
Understand how pictures become numbers.
Solve word problems about image recognition.
Know that image AI can make mistakes and why.
Respect privacy with photos and face recognition.
Explain features you use to recognise objects.

guide.what: Image recognition AI learns from thousands of labelled photos. It finds features like ears, wings or shapes, then guesses what is in a new picture. It can be wrong when photos are blurry, unusual or different from what it learned. Photos of people are private, so we ask before taking or sharing them.
steps: Play 'guess from one feature': describe a tail or an ear and let your child guess the animal.
Try photo search on a phone (for example 'cat') and see what it finds.
Talk about asking before taking someone's photo.
home: Make a pixel picture on squared paper and write it as 1s and 0s.
Collect 10 leaf photos and sort them into healthy and not healthy.
guide.watch: If your child uses face unlock, explain that faces are private data, just like a password.

title: AI and creativity Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on ai and creativity, from "Can AI Be Creative?" to "My Creative Plan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI can remix ideas, but people bring feelings and meaning.
Tell apart human, AI and shared creative work.
Name tools people use to create.
Use AI in creative work honestly.
Sequence a creative process that uses AI as a helper.
Learn words about creative work.
Use rhyme and pattern, like a poet.
Solve word problems about art and making.
Think about what makes human art special.
Plan creative work and use AI honestly.

guide.what: AI can make pictures, poems and music by mixing patterns it learned from people's work. It can be a helpful tool for ideas and checking. But people bring feelings, memories and choices to their art. When we use AI, we say so, make the work our own and never copy someone else's art.
steps: Make something together without any screens: a poem, a drawing or a song.
If you try an AI picture tool together, talk about who the ideas came from.
Practise saying 'I used AI for ideas' honestly.
home: Write a 4-line poem about your home, then draw it.
Visit a craft bazaar or look at truck art and talk about the artists.
guide.watch: Children may feel AI art is 'better'. Praise effort, choices and personal meaning in their own work.

title: Deepfakes and fake news Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on deepfakes and fake news, from "Real or Fake?" to "My Detective Badge". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what deepfakes and fake news are.
Find warning signs in posts and videos.
Follow a simple routine before sharing.
Judge headlines carefully.
Learn words about checking information.
Tell facts from opinions.
See how sharing makes stories spread fast.
Understand that fake news can hurt people.
Choose what to do with a suspicious post.
Write your own rules for spotting fakes.

guide.what: A deepfake is a fake photo, video or voice made with AI. Fake news is a made-up story shared as true. They spread fast and can hurt real people. Before believing or sharing, we stop, think about the source, check trusted places and ask a grown-up.
steps: Look at a family WhatsApp forward together and check it.
Practise the STOP steps with a silly headline.
Talk about the difference between fact and opinion at the dinner table.
home: Make a 'Think before you share' poster for the fridge.
Write two headlines, one true and one fake, and let the family guess.
guide.watch: Keep it calm: the aim is careful thinking, not fear. Show your child that grown-ups check too.

title: AI and jobs Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on ai and jobs, from "AI at Work" to "My Future Job". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that AI helps with some tasks while people do many jobs.
Name jobs people do.
Compare the strengths of AI and people.
Link jobs to helpful AI tools.
Know that technology creates new kinds of jobs.
Know the skills people need with AI around.
Solve word problems about AI at work.
Sequence how a person and AI share a task.
Learn about real jobs and technology.
Imagine future work with AI as a helper.

guide.what: AI is good at fast, repeated tasks like sorting and counting. People are good at caring, creating, solving new problems and making fair choices. In many jobs, people and AI work together, and technology also creates new jobs. Learning, kindness and checking facts will always matter.
steps: Talk about the tools and apps you use in your own work.
Ask your child: what part of a job needs a person?
Visit a workplace or shop and spot the machines that help.
home: Interview a relative about their job.
Make a 'jobs of the future' poster with three new job ideas.
guide.watch: Some children hear that 'robots will take all the jobs'. Reassure them: people and tools have always worked together, and caring and creative skills matter most.

title: Machine learning steps Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on machine learning steps, from "How Machines Learn" to "Design a Model". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the main steps of machine learning.
Sequence the steps of machine learning.
Tell rule-based programs from learning programs.
Train a 'human model' with labelled examples.
Understand why we test on new data.
Learn machine learning words.
Work out how often a model is right.
Label data into categories.
See how wrong labels confuse a model.
Plan the steps of a simple ML project.

guide.what: Machine learning is how computers learn from examples instead of following rules written for every case. People collect data, label it, train a model, test it on new examples and improve it. Careful labels, lots of examples and fair testing make a model better.
steps: Play 'train the model' with picture cards: give labelled examples, then test with new ones.
Ask: was this program told a rule, or did it learn?
Talk about why testing on new examples matters, like a surprise quiz.
home: Sort 20 household items into two labels and see if a sibling can learn your rule.
Keep a tally of how often a guessing game is right.
guide.watch: Use the word 'model' for the part that learned, so it stays a tool and not a 'brain'.

title: Translation and languages Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on translation and languages, from "Machines That Translate" to "My Language Map". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know how AI translation works and its limits.
Match everyday words in Urdu and English.
Know some of Pakistan's languages.
See why word-for-word translation can go wrong.
Choose when machine translation is enough.
Sequence how a translation app works.
Solve word problems about languages.
Choose translations that keep the meaning.
Know greetings in different languages.
Celebrate the languages you know.

guide.what: Translation apps change words from one language to another. They learned from millions of sentences that people had already translated. They are useful for signs, menus and simple questions, but can get idioms, poems and important messages wrong. A person who knows both languages should check anything important.
steps: Talk about the languages spoken by grandparents and relatives.
Try a translation app with a simple sentence, then with an idiom, and compare.
Teach your child one saying in your home language and its meaning.
home: Make a family 'hello' chart in every language you know.
Translate a short note into Urdu together and check it with an elder.
guide.watch: Celebrate every language your child hears at home. Speaking more than one language is a real strength.

title: Sounds f, b, e, h Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Nursery English practice on sounds f, b, e, h, from "The Sound f" to "My b Picture". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hear and write the f sound.
Trace small f and capital F.
Hear and write the b sound.
Trace small b and capital B.
Hear the short e sound at the start of words.
Trace small e and capital E.
Hear and write the h sound.
Trace small h and capital H.
Tell apart the sounds f, b, e and h.
Think of words that start with b.

guide.what: Four new letter sounds: f as in fish, b as in banana, e as in egg and h as in horse. Children hear the sound, trace the letter and find words that start with it.
steps: Say the sound, not the letter name: /b/ not 'bee'.
Feel the puff of air for /h/ by holding a hand in front of your mouth.
Play I spy with the four sounds.
home: Hunt for things at home that start with b or h.
Make the letters with sticks, string or play dough.
guide.watch: Small b and d are easy to mix up. Show that b has its big tummy on the right, like a bat and then a ball.

title: Big and small, tall and short Practice
topic: Big and small, tall and short
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Nursery Maths practice on big and small, tall and short, from "Big and Small" to "Draw Big and Small". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use the words big and small.
Put things in order of size.
Use the words tall and short.
Put things in order of height.
Compare two things by size.
Use taller and shorter to compare.
Sort things by size.
Choose the right size word for a picture.
Count and compare in number stories.
Draw things of different sizes.
