pages.topic: Big and small, tall and short

guide.what: Comparing size: big and small, tall and short, bigger and taller. Children look, compare and put things in order from small to big.
steps: Use size words often: 'Pass me the big spoon.'
Line up family members from short to tall.
Compare two toys and ask which is bigger.
home: Sort shoes at home into big and small.
Stand next to a door and mark your child's height.
guide.watch: Tall is about height and big is about size. A long snake lying down is long, not tall.

title: Our helpers at home Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on our helpers at home, from "Who Helps at Home?" to "How I Help". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that many people help at home.
Know what helpers at home do.
Name helpers at home.
Match tools to jobs at home.
Find ways to help at home.
Thank the people who help us.
Put the jobs of a day in order.
Know how to stay safe when grown-ups are working.
Count in simple stories about home.
Show how you help at home.

guide.what: The people who help at home, such as Ammi, Abbu, a cook, a driver or a gardener, the tools they use, and the ways children can help too.
steps: Give your child one small job each day.
Say thank you to helpers in front of your child.
Talk about what each person at home does.
home: Make a simple helper chart with stickers.
Let your child help water plants or fold socks.
guide.watch: Every home is different. Some families do all the jobs themselves. Talk about everyone who helps, including the children.

title: دو حروف جوڑنا کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on joining two letters (دو حروف جوڑنا), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Join a letter with ا.
Trace joined letters.
Join two letters to make short words.
Find the two letters in a short word.
Know letters that do not join forward.
Trace two letter words.
Read two letter words with pictures.
Match letters to the joined word.
Count letters in short words.
Write and draw a two letter word.

guide.what: Joining two Urdu letters: the first letter gets shorter when it joins (ب + ا = با), short words like بس، دل and گل, and the letters that do not join forward (ا، د، ر، ز، و).
steps: Write the two letters apart, then show them joined.
Say each letter, then say the joined sound.
Point out letters that never hold hands with the next letter.
home: Find بس and دل on signs, packets or in books.
Join letters with a finger on a misty window.
guide.watch: Children often write the full shape of the first letter. Show that ب becomes a small hook before it joins.

title: Blends bl, cl, fl Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of KG English practice on blends bl, cl, fl, from "What Is a Blend?" to "My Blend Sentence". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hear the blends bl, cl and fl at the start of words.
Read and write bl words.
Read and write cl words.
Read and write fl words.
Blend sounds to read new words.
Sort words by their blend.
Use blend words in sentences.
Read a short text with blend words.
Spot bl, cl and fl words in a sentence.
Write a sentence using a blend word.

guide.what: A blend is two consonant sounds said together quickly, where we can still hear both: bl as in blue, cl as in clock and fl as in flag.
steps: Say the two sounds slowly, then faster until they blend.
Clap once for the blend and once for the rest of the word.
Point out blends on signs and packets.
home: Make a bl, cl, fl word list on the fridge.
Play I spy with blends: I spy a cl... clock!
guide.watch: Some children drop the l and say 'fag' for flag or 'cap' for clap. Stretch the l sound to help.

title: Number bonds to 10 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of KG Maths practice on number bonds to 10, from "What Is a Number Bond?" to "Draw a Bond". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that two parts make a whole.
Know all the number bonds to 5.
Know all the number bonds to 10.
Find the missing part of a whole.
Use pictures to find bonds to 10.
Spot pairs of numbers that make 10.
Recall pairs that make 10.
Solve number stories with bonds to 10.
Use fingers to find bonds to 10.
Show a number bond to 10 in a drawing.

guide.what: Number bonds are pairs of numbers that make a whole. Children learn the bonds to 5 and to 10 (like 7 and 3, or 6 and 4) using fingers, pictures and stories.
steps: Use 10 fingers: put some down and count the rest.
Ask quick questions: 'I have 6. How many more make 10?'
Say each bond as a pair: 'seven and three make ten'.
home: Hide some of 10 buttons under a cup. Ask how many are hidden.
Play a bond snap game with number cards.
guide.watch: Children often count every time. Practise the pairs until they know them by heart, like a rhyme.

title: Food we eat Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on food we eat, from "Why We Eat" to "My Healthy Plate". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that food helps us grow and play.
Name common foods.
Know which foods to eat every day and which only now and then.
Know where some foods come from.
Know that food comes from plants and animals.
Know the three main meals of the day.
Know healthy habits at mealtimes.
Read about a family meal.
Use numbers to answer food questions.
Plan a healthy meal.

guide.what: The food we eat and why: fruit and vegetables, everyday and sometimes foods, where food comes from, the three meals of the day and good eating habits.
steps: Name foods in English and Urdu at mealtimes.
Let your child choose a fruit or vegetable at the shop.
Talk about where milk, eggs and roti come from.
home: Make a fruit salad together.
Draw a meal plan for one day.
guide.watch: Keep talk about food kind and calm. Say 'sometimes food' rather than 'bad food'.

title: آسان جملے کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of KG Urdu practice on simple sentences (آسان جملے), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know that a sentence tells a whole idea.
Write simple sentences about pictures.
Finish a sentence with a describing word.
Use ہے for one and ہیں for many.
Match the parts of a sentence.
Choose the sentence with the right word order.
Read short sentences and answer questions.
Finish simple sentences.
Read number sentences in Urdu.
Write your own simple sentences.

guide.what: Simple Urdu sentences: words join to make a sentence that ends with ۔, using یہ and وہ, describing words, and ہے for one thing and ہیں for many.
steps: Point to things at home and say a sentence: یہ کرسی ہے۔
Ask your child to finish your sentence.
Show the full stop ۔ at the end of each sentence.
home: Make picture cards and say one sentence for each.
Read a short Urdu story and count the sentences.
guide.watch: Children may say ہے for everything. Show one goat and many goats to explain ہیں.

title: Simple apps on a tablet Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 ICT practice on simple apps on a tablet, from "What Is a Tablet?" to "My Tablet Screen". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a tablet, an icon and an app are.
Know the touch moves for a tablet.
Know what some apps are for.
Choose the right touch move for a job.
Follow the steps to open and close an app.
Know how to look after a tablet's battery.
Know how to use a tablet carefully.
Tell apps apart from real objects.
Use maths in tablet stories.
Plan and draw your own home screen.

guide.what: Using a tablet: icons and apps, touch moves like tap, swipe and pinch, opening and closing an app, the battery icon and looking after the tablet.
steps: Show your child how to tap, swipe and pinch on a photo.
Name each app icon together and say what it does.
Agree a time limit before using the tablet.
home: Take three photos together and swipe through them.
Draw a picture in a drawing app, then close it with the Home button.
guide.watch: Children may tap too hard or too long and move icons by mistake. Show a light, quick tap.

title: Similes Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 English practice on similes, from "What Is a Simile?" to "My Simile Poem". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a simile compares two things using like or as.
Complete well-known similes with as.
Match similes to pictures.
Complete similes that use like.
Choose like or as in a simile.
Find the two things in a simile.
Find similes in a poem.
Sort similes by the word they use.
Write new similes.
Use similes in your own writing.

guide.what: Similes compare two things using like or as: as brave as a lion, sings like a bird. They help readers picture an idea.
steps: Find the two things being compared in each simile.
Ask: does it use like or as?
Make up a funny simile together for someone in the family.
home: On a walk, describe things with similes: the cloud is like a sheep.
Hunt for similes in a storybook or poem.
guide.watch: A sentence with like is not always a simile. I like rice is not comparing anything.

title: Adding and subtracting with regrouping Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on adding and subtracting with regrouping, from "Carrying a Ten" to "Number Puzzles". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Add 2-digit numbers, carrying into the tens.
Add 3-digit numbers with regrouping.
Subtract 2-digit numbers with regrouping.
Subtract 3-digit numbers with regrouping.
Decide when regrouping is needed.
Check subtraction with addition.
Solve word problems with regrouping.
Use regrouping to find missing digits.
Find and fix regrouping mistakes.
Use adding and subtracting to solve puzzles.

guide.what: Adding and subtracting within 1000 when we need to carry (regroup 10 ones as 1 ten, or 10 tens as 1 hundred) or borrow (change 1 ten into 10 ones).
steps: Always start with the ones column.
Use bundles of 10 straws or matchsticks to show carrying and borrowing.
Check each take-away by adding the answer back.
home: Add up two shop prices together and work out the change.
Write a sum with a mistake and let your child find it.
guide.watch: In subtraction, children often take the smaller digit from the bigger one (52 − 27 = 35). Remind them to borrow when the top digit is smaller.

title: Hot and cold Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on hot and cold, from "Hot or Cold?" to "Ice Cube Race". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that things can be hot or cold.
Sort things into hot and cold.
Say if things in pictures are hot or cold.
Know that temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.
Know that heat melts ice and cold freezes water.
Know that heat moves from hot things to cold things.
Know how clothes keep us warm in winter.
Know how to stay safe near hot things.
Use maths to compare temperatures.
Plan a fair test about melting.

guide.what: Hot and cold: heat, using a thermometer and degrees Celsius, melting and freezing, how heat moves from hot to cold, keeping warm in winter and staying safe near hot things.
steps: Feel a cup of warm water and a cup of cold water, then talk about which has more heat.
Read a thermometer together each morning for a week.
Talk about stove and kettle safety.
home: Do the ice cube race on a sunny day.
Put a metal spoon and a wooden spoon in warm water and feel which gets warm.
guide.watch: Children often think a coat makes heat. It does not; it traps the heat our body already makes.

title: Ancient India and Gandhara art Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 History practice on ancient india and gandhara art, from "The Land of Gandhara" to "Little Archaeologist". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know where and when Gandhara was.
Put times in our history in order.
Know that people came to Gandhara from far away.
Describe Gandhara art.
Know that Taxila was a famous place of learning.
Know where we can see Gandhara heritage today.
Compare life long ago with today.
Know how to look after our heritage.
Use maths with history facts.
Imagine and write about an old object.

guide.what: Gandhara, the ancient land around Peshawar, Taxila and Swat; visitors such as Alexander the Great and Silk Road traders; Gandhara stone art with calm faces and wavy folds; learning at Taxila; and caring for our heritage.
steps: Find Peshawar, Taxila, Mardan and Swat on a map.
Look at photos of Gandhara carvings and talk about the wavy cloth folds.
Make a family timeline next to the history timeline.
home: Visit the Taxila Museum, the Peshawar Museum or the Lahore Museum if you can.
Make a small carving from a bar of soap with a blunt plastic knife.
guide.watch: Children may mix up Harappa and Gandhara. Harappa is much older (about 4500 years ago); Gandhara was famous about 2000 years ago.

title: Mountains of Pakistan Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on mountains of pakistan, from "Our High Mountains" to "My Mountain Trip". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that Pakistan has very high mountains in the north.
Name the highest mountains in Pakistan.
Name the parts of a mountain.
Know animals that live in our mountains.
Know that mountain snow gives water to rivers.
Describe life in mountain areas.
Know mountains and hills in different parts of Pakistan.
Compare mountains and plains.
Use maths with mountain facts.
Plan a trip to the mountains.

guide.what: Pakistan's mountains: the Karakoram, Himalayas and Hindu Kush, K2, Nanga Parbat and Tirich Mir, parts of a mountain, mountain animals such as the markhor and snow leopard, and how melting snow feeds our rivers.
steps: Find the northern areas, K2 and the Indus River on a map of Pakistan.
Look at photos of K2 and the Karakoram Highway together.
Talk about why it is colder high up a mountain.
home: Build a mountain from a pile of clay or sand and name its parts.
Freeze some water in a tray, let it melt on a slope and watch it run downhill like a river.
guide.watch: Children often think the highest mountain in the world is in Pakistan. K2 is the second highest; Mount Everest in Nepal is the highest.

title: Money and saving Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on money and saving, from "Our Money" to "My Money Box". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that Pakistan's money is the rupee.
Know Pakistani coins and notes.
Tell needs and wants apart.
Know ways to save money.
Know what a bank does.
Plan how to save for something.
Solve money word problems.
Plan spending with a budget.
Know good habits with money.
Make a personal saving plan.

guide.what: Money and saving: the Pakistani rupee, coins and notes, needs and wants, what a bank does, saving goals and spending within a budget.
steps: Let your child sort real coins and notes by value.
Talk about needs and wants when you go shopping.
Help your child choose a small saving goal.
home: Set up a money box and mark progress on a chart each week.
Give a small budget at the shop and let your child plan what to buy.
guide.watch: Children may think more coins always means more money. Show that one Rs 100 note is worth more than five Rs 10 coins.

title: صفت کے الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on describing words (صفت کے الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know that an adjective describes a noun.
Use colour adjectives.
Know adjectives with opposite meanings.
Tell nouns and adjectives apart.
Match things to adjectives of taste and touch.
Match the adjective to the noun.
Use adjectives in sentences.
Find adjectives in a short passage.
Read Urdu number stories with adjectives.
Write sentences with adjectives.

guide.what: Adjectives (صفت) in Urdu: words that describe a noun, such as لال سیب، بڑا ہاتھی. Children find adjectives, use colour words, learn opposites and match the adjective ending to the noun (اچھا لڑکا، اچھی لڑکی، اچھے بچے).
steps: Point to things at home and ask: یہ کیسا ہے؟
Practise opposite pairs: بڑا، چھوٹا؛ گرم، ٹھنڈا.
Notice how some adjectives change with the noun: کالا گھوڑا، کالی بلی.
home: Play a guessing game: describe a fruit with two adjectives and let your child guess it.
Read a short Urdu story and underline the adjectives.
guide.watch: Some adjectives change with the noun (اچھا، اچھی، اچھے) and some do not (نرم، سخت، خوبصورت). Let children hear both kinds.

title: Simple slides Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 ICT practice on simple slides, from "What Is a Slide?" to "My Slide Checklist". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what slides and presentations are.
Name the parts of a slide.
Follow the steps to make a slide.
Know what makes a slide easy to read.
Use buttons in a slides app.
Put slides in a sensible order.
Plan slides before making them.
Use maths with slides.
Know how to present slides well.
Check a slide show before sharing it.

guide.what: Making simple slides: what a slide and a presentation are, parts of a slide (title, text box, picture, slide number), making and saving a slide, good slide design and presenting well.
steps: Plan the slides on paper first, then make them on a computer or tablet.
Keep words short and big.
Let your child present the slides to the family.
home: Make a 3-slide show about a family trip with one photo on each slide.
Watch your child present and clap at the end!
guide.watch: Children often put too many words on a slide. One idea and one picture per slide is best.

title: Figurative language Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 English practice on figurative language, from "Words That Paint Pictures" to "Write with Figurative Language". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that figurative language does not mean exactly what it says.
Tell similes and metaphors apart.
Complete common similes.
Spot human actions given to things.
Use onomatopoeia and alliteration.
Know that hyperbole is a huge exaggeration.
Understand common English idioms.
Identify similes, metaphors, personification and hyperbole.
Find figurative language in a poem.
Use figurative language in your own writing.

guide.what: Figurative language at Grade 4 level: similes (like, as), metaphors, personification, onomatopoeia, alliteration, hyperbole and common idioms, then finding them in a poem and using them in writing.
steps: Explain that figurative words make pictures in the mind and are not meant literally.
Spot similes and metaphors together in story books and poems.
Ask your child to turn a plain sentence into a figurative one: The rain fell → The rain drummed on the roof.
home: Play idiom charades: act out an idiom literally (raining cats and dogs) and guess it.
Write a family list of Urdu sayings and talk about their real meanings.
guide.watch: Children often mix up similes and metaphors. A simile uses like or as; a metaphor says one thing is another. Idioms should not be read word for word.

title: Long division basics Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on long division basics, from "Sharing and Grouping" to "Number Detective". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that division is sharing or grouping.
Use multiplication facts to divide.
Divide with remainders.
Divide multiples of 10.
Divide a 2-digit number by partitioning.
Use short division.
Use division in real life.
Decide what to do with a remainder.
Use the inverse to check division.
Reason about division.

guide.what: Long division basics: sharing and grouping, fact families, remainders, dividing multiples of 10, partitioning, short division (the bus stop method), word problems where you round up or down, and checking by multiplying.
steps: Make sure times tables to 10 × 10 are quick, since every division uses them.
Share real things (sweets, pencils) and talk about what is left over.
Always check a division by multiplying back.
home: Share a packet of biscuits equally among the family and talk about the remainder.
Work out how many cars are needed for a family trip if each car holds 5 people.
guide.watch: Children often forget to carry the leftover ten in short division, or give a remainder bigger than the divisor. In word problems they may forget to round up when everyone must fit.

title: Teeth and digestion Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on teeth and digestion, from "Why We Have Teeth" to "My Healthy Teeth Plan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know why we have teeth and how many.
Know incisors, canines and molars.
Name the parts of a tooth.
Know how to keep teeth healthy.
Know what digestion does.
Order the parts of the digestive system.
Know the job of each part of the digestive system.
Know habits that help digestion.
Use maths with body facts.
Plan habits for healthy teeth and digestion.

guide.what: Teeth and digestion: milk teeth and adult teeth, incisors, canines and molars, parts of a tooth (enamel, dentine, pulp, root), tooth decay and care, and the journey of food through the mouth, food pipe, stomach, small and large intestines.
steps: Look at teeth in a mirror together and find incisors, canines and molars.
Time two minutes of brushing with a timer or song.
Talk about where lunch goes after you swallow it.
home: Keep a two-week brushing chart and tick it morning and night.
Chew a piece of bread slowly and notice it turning sweet and soft, because saliva starts digestion.
guide.watch: Children often think digestion happens only in the stomach. Most goodness passes into the blood in the small intestine. They may also think milk teeth do not matter, but they hold space for adult teeth.

title: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 History practice on sir syed ahmad khan, from "Who Was Sir Syed?" to "Be a Historian". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know who Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was.
Order the main events of Sir Syed's life.
Know why Sir Syed worked for education.
Know about the school Sir Syed started.
Know about the Scientific Society and Sir Syed's magazine.
Know what the Aligarh Movement was.
Recall facts about Sir Syed.
Compare learning in Sir Syed's time and today.
Use dates to work out time.
Explain why Sir Syed is important.

guide.what: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (1817 to 1898): his life, the effects of 1857, his belief in modern education and English, the Scientific Society, the magazine Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq, Aligarh College (later Aligarh Muslim University) and the Aligarh Movement.
steps: Find Delhi and Aligarh on a map of South Asia.
Talk about why learning English and science helped people get jobs then and now.
Make a simple timeline of Sir Syed's life together.
home: Visit a library and choose a book that was translated from another language.
Ask grandparents about their school days and compare them with today.
guide.watch: Children may think Sir Syed lived at the time of Pakistan's creation. He died in 1898, almost 50 years before 1947, but his students and ideas helped the Pakistan Movement.

title: Natural resources of Pakistan Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on natural resources of pakistan, from "Gifts from Nature" to "Resource Fact File". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what natural resources are.
Tell renewable and non-renewable resources apart.
Know how Pakistan uses its rivers.
Know Pakistan's main minerals and fuels.
Know about a famous resource in Pakistan.
Know where Pakistan's forests are and why they matter.
Use a map to find resources.
Know how to look after resources.
Use maths to think about resources.
Present facts about a natural resource.

guide.what: Natural resources of Pakistan: renewable and non-renewable resources, rivers, canals and dams (Tarbela, Mangla), minerals and fuels (Khewra salt, Thar coal, Sui gas, Reko Diq copper and gold, oil), forests and mangroves, and using resources wisely.
steps: Look at things at home and ask where they came from in nature: salt, gas for cooking, wooden chairs.
Find the Indus, Tarbela and Khewra on a map of Pakistan.
Talk about which resources will run out one day.
home: Check the house for dripping taps and lights left on.
Taste a pinch of pink salt and plain salt and talk about where they come from.
guide.watch: Children often think water and gas will never run out. Water is renewable but can still be wasted or polluted, and gas, coal and oil will run out.

title: Our constitution Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on our constitution, from "What Is a Constitution?" to "Our Class Constitution". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a constitution is.
Compare class rules with rules for a country.
Know when Pakistan's constitution was made.
Know the main parts of government.
Know about the two houses of Parliament.
Know some rights the constitution gives us.
Know that citizens have duties too.
Know how the constitution can be changed.
Use dates and numbers about the constitution.
Apply the idea of rights and duties.

guide.what: Our constitution: what a constitution is, Pakistan's constitutions of 1956, 1962 and 1973, the parts of government (Parliament, Prime Minister, President, courts), the National Assembly and Senate, our rights (education, equality, speech, vote, property, movement), our duties, and amendments.
steps: Compare the constitution to family or class rules that everyone agrees to follow.
Talk about rights and the duties that go with them.
Watch a short news clip about Parliament and ask who makes laws.
home: Write a family constitution together with three rights and three duties.
Hold a family vote on a small choice and count whether two thirds agree.
guide.watch: Children may think the President makes all the laws. Parliament makes laws, the government runs the country and the courts check that laws are fair.

title: رموزِ اوقاف کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on punctuation (رموزِ اوقاف), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know the main Urdu punctuation marks.
Choose between ۔ and ؟
Sort questions and statements.
Use commas in a list.
Use the exclamation mark.
Write what someone said.
Recall where each mark is used.
Find punctuation marks in a passage.
Spot correct punctuation.
Use punctuation in your own writing.

guide.what: Punctuation in Urdu (رموزِ اوقاف): ختمہ (۔), سوالیہ نشان (؟), سکتہ (،), ندائیہ نشان (!), واوین (“ ”) and رابطہ (:). Children choose the right mark, sort questions and statements, fix mistakes and count marks in a short story.
steps: Read an Urdu sentence aloud and ask: is it a question or a statement?
Point out ؟ and ! in Urdu story books.
Show that Urdu's question mark faces the other way from the English one.
home: Write three family sentences on the fridge: one ending in ۔, one in ؟ and one in !.
Read a short Urdu dialogue together and spot the واوین.
guide.watch: Children sometimes use the English full stop (.) in Urdu instead of ختمہ (۔), or forget the question mark after کیا questions.

title: Making a poster Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 ICT practice on making a poster, from "What Makes a Good Poster?" to "Plan My Poster". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a poster is for.
Know why posters are made.
Name the parts of a poster.
Choose readable fonts and sizes.
Use colours with good contrast.
Know tools for making a poster on a computer.
Know how to use pictures fairly and safely.
Follow steps to make a poster.
Use measuring and money with posters.
Design a poster with a clear purpose.

guide.what: Making a poster: purpose and audience, parts of a poster (title, picture, details, slogan), font sizes, colour and contrast, computer tools such as text boxes and shapes, using pictures fairly, and the steps from sketch to print.
steps: Look at posters at school, in shops or on roads and ask what each one wants you to do.
Talk about whether the words are easy to read from far away.
Let your child try text boxes and shapes in a free design or slides app.
home: Make a poster for a family event, like a birthday or a clean-up day.
Hold a poster up across the room and check what can still be read.
guide.watch: Children often fill every space with words and colours. A good poster has white space, a few big words and one clear picture.

words: to tell people about an event
to make people change a habit

title: Big and small letters Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Nursery English practice on big and small letters, from "Two Ways to Write" to "My Name". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that each letter has a big and a small shape.
Trace big and small letters side by side.
Match big letters to small letters.
Spot letters where big and small look alike.
Write the capital letter for a first sound.
Know that names start with a big letter.
Tell big letters from small letters.
Sort big and small letters.
Count the capital letters in names.
Write your own name with a big first letter.

guide.what: Every letter has a big (capital) shape and a small shape that make the same sound. Children match pairs like A and a, and learn that names start with a big letter.
steps: Point to big and small letters in a story book.
Say 'big A, small a' as you trace.
Write your child's name with a big first letter for them to copy.
home: Make letter pairs on cards and play snap.
Find big letters on shop signs and packets.
guide.watch: Some pairs look very different, like G and g or H and h. Practise these more.

obj: Name circles, squares and triangles.
Trace circles, squares and triangles.
Find shapes in things around us.
Count the sides of a square and a triangle.
Name and colour circles, squares and triangles.
Sort things by shape.
Count groups of shapes.
Use shape words in sentences.
Count shapes in number stories.
Use shapes to make a picture.

guide.what: Circles, squares and triangles in the world around us: a coin is a circle, a window is a square and a flag can be a triangle. Children count sides and corners and find shapes at home.
steps: Go on a shape walk at home and name each shape.
Run a finger round the edge of a plate and along a book.
Count the sides out loud: one, two, three.
home: Cut a roti or sandwich into triangles and squares.
Make shapes with sticks, straws or ice lolly sticks.
guide.watch: A square turned on its corner is still a square. Turn shapes around so children see this.

title: Winter in Pakistan Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on winter in pakistan, from "Winter Is Here" to "Me in Winter". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what winter feels like.
Name warm winter clothes.
Tell winter things from summer things.
Know that it snows in the north of Pakistan.
Name foods we eat in winter.
Stay safe on foggy winter days.
Know how we keep warm in winter.
Put getting ready on a cold day in order.
Count in winter stories.
Show how you dress in winter.

guide.what: Winter in Pakistan: cold days, warm clothes, snow in the mountains, foggy mornings and winter foods like peanuts, oranges and carrot halwa.
steps: Talk about the weather each morning: is it cold today?
Name each warm thing as your child puts it on.
Look at pictures of snow in Murree or Swat.
home: Eat peanuts or an orange together and count them.
Feel an ice cube and talk about cold.
guide.watch: Children may want to stand close to heaters. Show a safe distance and keep them out of reach.

title: تصویر والے دو حرفی الفاظ کی مشق
en: Two letter words with pictures practice
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on two letter words with pictures (تصویر والے دو حرفی الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read two letter words with pictures.
Trace two letter picture words.
Hear the first letter of a picture word.
Hear the last letter of a picture word.
Choose the word for a picture.
Join two letters to make a picture word.
Find the two letters in a picture word.
Spot a word among other words.
Read a tiny sentence with a picture word.
Write and draw a two letter word.

guide.what: Two letter Urdu words with pictures: آم، آگ، پر، کپ، ٹب and دو. Children hear the first and last letter, join two letters and read a tiny sentence like یہ آم ہے۔
steps: Point to the picture, say the word, then say each letter.
Ask: what is the first sound? What is the last sound?
Read یہ ... ہے with real things at home.
home: Show a real mango or cup and read its word card.
Make picture word cards and match them.
guide.watch: آ has a little hat (مد) on top. Children may forget it and write ا. Point to the hat each time.

title: Sentences with I can Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of KG English practice on sentences with i can, from "I Can!" to "My I Can Sentences". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Write simple sentences that start with I can.
Finish I can sentences with action words.
Use a capital I and a full stop.
Put words in order to make a sentence.
Use can and cannot about animals.
Read a short text with I can sentences.
Tell real actions from impossible ones.
Complete I can sentences.
Know that a sentence is made of words.
Write your own I can sentences.

guide.what: Writing simple sentences that start with I can. A sentence starts with a capital letter, ends with a full stop, and the word I is always a capital. Children also use cannot.
steps: Act out an action and say the sentence: 'I can jump.'
Point to the capital I and the full stop in each sentence.
Clap once for each word as you read.
home: Make an 'I can' poster with photos of your child.
Take turns: 'I can ...' and your child copies the action.
guide.watch: Children often write a small i for I. Remind them that I on its own is always tall.

title: Adding and taking away stories Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of KG Maths practice on adding and taking away stories, from "Put Together, Take Away" to "My Number Story". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what adding and taking away mean.
Add two groups in a picture story.
Take away in a picture story.
Choose the right action for a story.
Add numbers up to 10.
Take away within 10.
Solve adding stories.
Solve taking away stories.
Follow a story with adding and taking away.
Make up an adding or taking away story.

guide.what: Adding and taking away in everyday stories. Adding puts groups together to get more; taking away means some go and fewer are left. Children write sums with + and -.
steps: Act out stories with toys: 3 cars, 2 more drive in.
Ask: will we have more or fewer?
Say the number sentence after each story.
home: Use snacks at teatime for adding and taking away stories.
Make up a story on the way to school and solve it together.
guide.watch: Children may add when a story says 'left' or 'eaten'. Ask: did the group get bigger or smaller?

title: Clothes for each season Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on clothes for each season, from "Weather and Clothes" to "Dress for a Season". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that we dress for the weather.
Name clothes and things we wear.
Choose clothes for the weather.
Know which cloth keeps us cool or warm.
Sort clothes by season.
Use clothes words in sentences.
Read about packing for cold weather.
Put on winter clothes in the right order.
Count in clothes stories.
Choose and draw clothes for a season.

guide.what: Clothes for summer, winter and the rainy season: light cotton clothes for heat, warm wool for cold, and an umbrella or raincoat for rain.
steps: Check the weather each morning and choose clothes together.
Feel a cotton shirt and a wool sweater and compare.
Let your child pack a small bag for a pretend trip.
home: Sort a pile of clothes into summer and winter.
Dress a teddy for rain, sun and snow.
guide.watch: Children may think thick clothes are always better. Talk about how we feel too hot in a coat in summer.

title: رنگ اور شکلیں کی مشق
en: Colours and shapes in Urdu practice
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of KG Urdu practice on colours and shapes in urdu (رنگ اور شکلیں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Name the main colours in Urdu.
Name more colours in Urdu.
Match Urdu colour words to English.
Say the colour of things in Urdu.
Name shapes in Urdu.
Trace shapes and say their Urdu names.
Use colour words in sentences.
Sort colour words and shape words.
Count coloured things in Urdu sentences.
Draw a picture using shapes and colours.

guide.what: Colours in Urdu (لال، پیلا، نیلا، ہرا، کالا، سفید، نارنجی، جامنی، بھورا) and shapes (دائرہ، چوکور، تکون), used in short sentences.
steps: Name colours in Urdu while getting dressed.
Find a دائرہ، چوکور and تکون in the kitchen.
Say a sentence: آسمان نیلا ہے۔
home: Play I spy in Urdu: میں ایک لال چیز دیکھ رہا ہوں۔
Sort crayons and say each colour in Urdu.
guide.watch: Some colour words change with the thing: ہرا پتا but ہری گھاس, پیلا سورج but پیلی گیند. Say both forms.

title: Pictures and sounds on a computer Practice
topic: Pictures and sounds on a computer
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 ICT practice on pictures and sounds on a computer, from "Seeing and Hearing" to "My Computer Picture". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that computers can show pictures and play sounds.
Name devices for pictures and sounds.
Tell input devices from output devices.
Change the volume of sounds.
Follow the steps to take a photo on a tablet.
Match a device to its job.
Use headphones and sounds safely.
Know the tools in a drawing app.
Use maths in computer stories.
Plan a picture and a sound for a computer project.
