guide.what: How computers show pictures and play sounds: screens, speakers, headphones, microphones, cameras and printers, input and output, changing the volume, taking a photo and drawing app tools.
steps: Find the speakers, microphone and camera on your phone or laptop.
Record your child saying a sentence and play it back.
Show the volume buttons and the mute button.
home: Take three photos together and choose the best one.
Draw a picture in a drawing app using the fill tool.
guide.watch: Children often turn the volume right up. Teach them to start low and turn it up a little at a time.

title: Fact and opinion Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 English practice on fact and opinion, from "What Is a Fact?" to "Facts and My Opinion". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the difference between a fact and an opinion.
Test a sentence by asking if it can be checked.
Spot words that show an opinion.
Write facts about pictures.
Sort sentences into facts and opinions.
Tell facts from opinions about animals.
Find facts and opinions in a passage.
Turn an opinion into a fact.
Use maths facts in word problems.
Write facts and an opinion about a topic.

guide.what: Facts are true and can be checked (A week has seven days). Opinions are what someone thinks or feels (Sunday is the best day). Opinion words include best, beautiful, boring and I think.
steps: Ask: can we check this in a book or by looking?
Look for opinion words like best, worst, I think.
Let your child say an opinion and you say a fact about the same thing.
home: Read an advert together and find the facts and the opinions.
At dinner, take turns saying one fact and one opinion about the food.
guide.watch: Children often think an opinion they agree with is a fact. Everyone agreeing that mangoes are tasty still does not make it a fact.

title: Multiplying by 3 and 4 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on multiplying by 3 and 4, from "Groups of 3" to "Make Your Own". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Understand multiplying by 3 as equal groups.
Learn the 3 times table to 3 × 10.
Count in steps of 3 and 4.
Use doubling twice to multiply by 4.
Learn the 4 times table to 4 × 10.
Write multiplication for real-life groups.
Know that multiplication can be done in any order.
Solve word problems multiplying by 3 and 4.
Check multiplication facts.
Show multiplication with drawings and stories.

guide.what: Multiplying by 3 and 4: equal groups, counting in 3s and 4s, the 3 and 4 times tables, doubling twice to multiply by 4, and swapping the numbers (3 × 4 = 4 × 3).
steps: Use buttons or beans to make equal groups.
Chant the tables together, then ask facts out of order.
Show that 4 × is double, then double again.
home: Count the legs of chairs, tables or animals around you in 4s.
Count wheels on rickshaws (3 each) when you are out.
guide.watch: Children may add instead of multiply (3 × 4 = 7). Ask them to draw the groups to see the answer.

title: Magnets Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on magnets, from "What Is a Magnet?" to "Magnet Fishing Game". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a magnet pulls some metals.
Predict which things a magnet attracts.
Sort materials into magnetic and non-magnetic.
Know that a magnet has two poles.
Know that like poles push and unlike poles pull.
Know that magnetism can pass through some materials.
Know how magnets are used in daily life.
Plan a test to find magnetic things.
Use maths in a magnet investigation.
Design a game that uses magnets.

guide.what: Magnets: what they attract (iron and steel), magnetic and non-magnetic materials, north and south poles, attract and repel, magnetism through paper, and how magnets help us every day.
steps: Let your child test things at home with a fridge magnet.
Ask them to guess first, then test.
Say attract for pull together and repel for push apart.
home: Make a magnet fishing game with paper fish and paper clips.
Move a paper clip across a sheet of card with a magnet underneath.
guide.watch: Children often think all metals stick to magnets. Aluminium foil, copper and gold do not; mainly iron and steel do.

title: Islamic golden age scholars Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 History practice on islamic golden age scholars, from "A Golden Age of Learning" to "My Big Question". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know about a time of great learning about 1200 years ago.
Know some great scholars and their work.
Know how Al-Khwarizmi changed maths.
Know about Ibn Sina's work in medicine.
Know that Ibn al-Haytham studied light and seeing.
Know that Al-Biruni measured the Earth from a hill in Punjab.
Link old discoveries to things we use today.
Know good habits that helped scholars learn.
Use maths with history facts.
Ask a question and plan how to investigate.

guide.what: The golden age of learning about 1000 to 1200 years ago: the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, Al-Khwarizmi (algebra and algorithms), Ibn Sina (medicine), Ibn al-Haytham (light and seeing), Al-Biruni (who measured the Earth at Nandana Fort in Pakistan) and Al-Jazari (machines).
steps: Find Baghdad, Cairo, Cordoba and Jhelum on a world map.
Talk about how scholars learned by asking and testing.
Link each scholar to something we use today.
home: Make a pinhole viewer from a shoe box to see light like Ibn al-Haytham.
Write a simple algorithm (set of steps) for making a sandwich.
guide.watch: Children may think these scholars invented the modern camera or computer. Their ideas helped later people build them.

title: Rivers and lakes Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on rivers and lakes, from "Rivers of Pakistan" to "My River Journey". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that the Indus is the main river of Pakistan.
Name the parts of a river.
Know the five rivers of Punjab.
Know some lakes of Pakistan.
Tell rivers, lakes and seas apart.
Know how rivers help people.
Know about big dams in Pakistan.
Know how to care for rivers and lakes.
Use maths with river facts.
Describe the journey of a river.

guide.what: Rivers and lakes of Pakistan: the Indus and its tributaries (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi and Sutlej), parts of a river (source, tributary, mouth, delta), famous lakes such as Saiful Muluk, Manchar, Keenjhar and Attabad, dams, and keeping water clean.
steps: Trace the Indus on a map of Pakistan from the mountains to the sea.
Name the rivers your family has seen or crossed.
Talk about where your tap water comes from.
home: Pour water down a sand slope and watch a little river and delta form.
Look at photos of Saiful Muluk and Attabad Lake together.
guide.watch: Children may think rivers flow from the sea to the mountains. Water always flows downhill, from the mountains to the sea.

title: Markets and shops Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on markets and shops, from "Buyers and Sellers" to "My Own Shop". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that markets are places where people buy and sell.
Know different kinds of markets.
Tell goods and services apart.
Know which shop sells which goods.
Know how food gets from the farm to the shop.
Know some famous markets in Pakistan.
Read a simple bill and work out change.
Know good manners and honesty in shops.
Plan shopping wisely.
Plan a shop and its prices.

guide.what: Markets and shops: buyers and sellers, kinds of markets (bazaar, supermarket, weekly market, online), goods and services, how food gets from the farm to the shop, famous bazaars of Pakistan, reading a bill and honest shopping.
steps: Take your child shopping and let them read the prices.
Talk about goods and services you pay for.
Let your child check the change.
home: Play shop at home with toy money and price tags.
Make a shopping list together before going to the bazaar.
guide.watch: Children often think shopkeepers make everything they sell. Talk about where goods come from before they reach the shop.

words: a small shop near our home

title: مختصر پیراگراف لکھنا کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on writing a short paragraph (مختصر پیراگراف لکھنا), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know that a paragraph is a few sentences about one idea.
Choose a good opening sentence.
Find the sentence that does not belong.
Use joining words in sentences.
Put sentences in order to make a paragraph.
Write sentences about pictures.
Read a model paragraph and find its parts.
Complete a paragraph with the right words.
Read and solve Urdu number stories.
Write a short paragraph of your own.

guide.what: Writing a short Urdu paragraph (پیراگراف): a few sentences about one idea, a clear first sentence, sentences in order, joining words (اور، لیکن، کیونکہ، پھر) and a full stop (۔) at the end of each sentence.
steps: Talk about the topic first, then write.
Ask your child to say each sentence aloud before writing it.
Check that every sentence is about the same thing.
home: Write a family paragraph together about a weekend trip.
Cut a paragraph into strips and let your child put it back in order.
guide.watch: Children often add sentences that are off the topic. Ask: is this sentence about the same thing?

words: سردی کا موسم آ گیا ہے۔

title: Block coding: sequences Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 ICT practice on block coding: sequences, from "What Is a Sequence?" to "Code a Path". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a sequence is a set of steps in order.
Order the steps of everyday tasks.
Know what common coding blocks do.
Follow arrow instructions on a grid.
Name directions on arrow blocks.
Find a bug in a sequence.
Build a sequence of blocks.
See that repeating steps can make code shorter.
Use maths with coding.
Plan and write your own arrow sequence.

guide.what: Block coding with sequences: steps in the right order, coding blocks (start, move, turn, say, stop), arrow codes on a grid, finding bugs (debugging) and using repeat to make code shorter.
steps: Act out arrow codes: your child gives you instructions to walk across the room.
Talk about the order of steps in daily jobs like making chai.
Try ScratchJr or a similar free block coding app together.
home: Draw a grid with chalk outside and play robot and coder.
Mix up the steps of a recipe and ask your child to fix the order.
guide.watch: Children often mix up left and right when the robot faces a different way. Turn your body to face the same way as the robot.

title: Persuasive writing Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 English practice on persuasive writing, from "What Is Persuasive Writing?" to "Write a Persuasive Poster". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that persuasive writing tries to change what the reader thinks or does.
Back up an opinion with a reason.
Tell facts from opinions in persuasive writing.
Use strong, emotive words to persuade.
Recognise rhetorical questions, repetition and the rule of three.
Use connectives to order and link arguments.
Find the features of a persuasive letter.
Recognise persuasive language in adverts.
Plan a persuasive piece with an opening, reasons and a conclusion.
Use persuasive tricks in your own writing.

guide.what: Persuasive writing at Grade 4 level: opinions and reasons, fact and opinion, emotive power words, rhetorical questions, repetition and the rule of three, linking words (firstly, furthermore, therefore, in conclusion), a persuasive letter, adverts and planning an argument.
steps: Look at adverts on TV, billboards or cereal boxes and ask: what do they want you to do, and which words try to persuade you?
When your child asks for something, ask them to give three reasons.
Talk about facts that can be checked and opinions that cannot.
home: Hold a friendly family debate: Is winter better than summer? Each side gives three reasons.
Write a persuasive letter to a family member asking for a special day out.
guide.watch: Children often give opinions without reasons, or repeat the same reason in different words. They may also forget the conclusion that says their opinion again.

title: Equivalent fractions Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on equivalent fractions, from "Fractions Are Equal Parts" to "Fraction Challenge". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Revise numerators and denominators.
Know that equivalent fractions show the same amount.
Use a fraction wall to find equivalent fractions.
Find equivalent fractions by multiplying.
Simplify fractions by dividing.
Find equivalent fractions in real life.
Find fractions of an amount.
Compare fractions using equivalents.
Solve problems with equivalent fractions.
Reason about equivalent fractions.

guide.what: Equivalent fractions: numerators and denominators, fractions that show the same amount, the fraction wall, multiplying and dividing top and bottom by the same number, simplest form, fractions of amounts and comparing fractions.
steps: Fold paper strips into halves, quarters and eighths and line them up to see equal amounts.
Cut a roti or a pizza and ask: is 2 out of 4 the same as 1 out of 2?
Remind your child: do the same to the top and the bottom.
home: Share a pack of biscuits and ask what fraction each person gets.
Make a fraction wall from coloured paper and stick it on the fridge.
guide.watch: Children often think 1/8 is bigger than 1/4 because 8 is bigger than 4. More parts means each part is smaller. They may also add the same number to top and bottom instead of multiplying.

title: Light and reflection Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on light and reflection, from "Light Sources" to "Shadow Investigation". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that light comes from light sources.
Know that light travels in straight lines.
Know transparent, translucent and opaque materials.
Know how shadows are made.
Know that light bounces off surfaces.
Know how mirror images look.
Know everyday uses of mirrors and reflection.
Order how we see a reflection.
Use maths with light and shadows.
Plan a fair test about shadows.

guide.what: Light and reflection: light sources, light travelling in straight lines, transparent, translucent and opaque materials, how shadows form and change during the day, reflection, mirror images and everyday uses of mirrors such as periscopes and car mirrors.
steps: Go round the house and sort things into light sources and things that only reflect light.
Use a torch in a dark room to make shadow puppets.
Write your name and hold it up to a mirror.
home: Measure your own shadow in the morning, at midday and in the evening.
Make a simple periscope from a juice carton and two small mirrors (with a grown-up).
guide.watch: Children often think the Moon makes its own light, or that we see because light comes out of our eyes. Light comes from a source, bounces off things and enters our eyes.

title: Fatima Jinnah Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 History practice on fatima jinnah, from "Who Was Fatima Jinnah?" to "Be a Historian". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know who Fatima Jinnah was.
Order the main events of Fatima Jinnah's life.
Know about Fatima Jinnah's education and work.
Know how Fatima Jinnah helped her brother.
Know how Fatima Jinnah brought women into the Pakistan Movement.
Know why she is called the Mother of the Nation.
Know how Pakistan remembers Fatima Jinnah.
Recall facts about Fatima Jinnah.
Use dates to work out time.
Explain why Fatima Jinnah is important.

guide.what: Fatima Jinnah (1893 to 1967): her early life and education, her work as one of the first Muslim women dentists in South Asia, her support for the Quaid, bringing women into the Pakistan Movement, caring for refugees, the 1965 election and why she is called Madar-e-Millat.
steps: Look at pictures of Fatima Jinnah and the Quaid together in a book or online.
Talk about why it was brave for a girl to study at college in the 1910s and 1920s.
Find Karachi, Bombay (Mumbai) and Calcutta (Kolkata) on a map.
home: Visit Mazar-e-Quaid or a Fatima Jinnah Park, or look at pictures of them online.
Ask your child to name a woman in the family or community who inspires them and why.
guide.watch: Children sometimes mix up Fatima Jinnah with the Quaid's wife or daughter. She was his younger sister. They may also think she was a doctor for all illnesses: she was a dentist.

title: Population and cities Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on population and cities, from "What Is Population?" to "My City or Village". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what population means.
Know the difference between villages, towns and cities.
Know Pakistan's largest cities.
Use a map to locate cities.
Know why people move to cities.
Know the good things and problems of big cities.
Know what population density means.
Think about how to make cities better.
Use maths with population.
Describe the place where you live.

guide.what: Population and cities: what population and a census are, rural and urban places, villages, towns and cities, Pakistan's biggest cities (Karachi, Lahore, Faisalabad, Islamabad, Peshawar), why cities grow (migration, ports, trade), the good things and problems of city life, population density, and ideas to improve cities.
steps: Find Pakistan's biggest cities on a map and talk about which ones you have visited.
Ask: do we live in a rural or urban area? How do you know?
Count how many people live in your street or building.
home: Ask grandparents where they grew up and whether they moved to a city.
Look out of the car window on a trip and spot changes from city to countryside.
guide.watch: Children may think the capital is the biggest city. Islamabad is the capital, but Karachi and Lahore have many more people.

title: Taxes and public services Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on taxes and public services, from "What Are Public Services?" to "If I Spent the Taxes". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what public services are.
Know what taxes are and why we pay them.
Know what taxes pay for.
Know some kinds of tax.
Tell public and private services apart.
Know about emergency public services.
Know how to care for public property.
Know that the government plans how to spend taxes.
Use maths with taxes.
Decide how to share money between public services.

guide.what: Taxes and public services: what public services are, what taxes are and why we pay them, where tax money goes, kinds of tax (income, sales, property), public and private services, emergency services such as Rescue 1122, caring for public property and the government budget.
steps: On a walk, spot public services: streetlights, roads, parks, government schools and hospitals.
Look at a shop receipt together and find the tax line.
Talk about why it matters that everyone pays their fair share.
home: Make a family budget for a day out with a set amount of money.
Pick up litter together in a park and talk about who pays to clean it.
guide.watch: Children may think public services are free because nobody pays at the door. They are paid for by everyone through taxes.

title: کہانی نویسی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on story writing (کہانی نویسی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know the parts of a story.
Find the characters and setting.
Sort sentences into beginning, middle and end.
Use linking words in a story.
Tell a story from a sequence of pictures.
Write dialogue in a story.
Match each story to its lesson.
Order the events of a story.
Expand an outline into a story.
Write a short story with a beginning, middle and end.

guide.what: Story writing in Urdu (کہانی نویسی): the parts of a story (عنوان، کردار، آغاز، درمیان، انجام، سبق), characters and setting, linking words (ایک دن، پھر، اچانک، آخرکار), a picture story, dialogue with واوین, matching stories to their lessons, ordering events and writing a story from an outline.
steps: Read an Urdu story together and ask: who are the characters, where does it happen, and what is the lesson?
Tell a story aloud using ایک دن, پھر and آخرکار.
Let your child tell the story first, then write it.
home: Take turns adding one sentence each to a family story at dinner.
Draw four pictures of a day out and write one Urdu sentence under each.
guide.watch: Children often write a beginning and then stop, or jump straight to the end. Remind them that the middle is where the problem happens and gets solved.

title: Coding with loops and conditions Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 ICT practice on coding with loops and conditions, from "Algorithms and Sequences" to "Design a Game". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Revise algorithms and sequences.
Know that a loop repeats instructions.
Spot repeated actions in everyday life.
Use loops to draw shapes.
Know that conditions help programs make choices.
Pair conditions with the right action.
Tell loops and conditions apart.
Trace a program with a loop and a condition.
Find and fix bugs in loops and conditions.
Plan a program using loops and conditions.

guide.what: Coding with loops and conditions: algorithms and sequences, repeat and forever loops, drawing shapes with loops, conditions with if ... then ... else, tracing code, telling loops from conditions, debugging and planning a simple game in a block coding app such as Scratch.
steps: Play a game of robot: your child gives you instructions with repeat and if, and you follow them exactly.
Spot loops in daily life: the washing machine spin, a song chorus, stairs.
Try the free Scratch or ScratchJr app together and use the repeat block.
home: Write an if ... then ... else plan for the morning: if it is cold, then wear a jumper, else wear a shirt.
Draw a square on paper by following 'repeat 4: move, turn'.
guide.watch: Children often count the steps wrongly in a loop (for example repeating 3 times for a square), or put a block outside the loop when it should be inside.

title: AI on the farm Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on ai on the farm, from "Smart Farming" to "Design a Farm Helper". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know how AI helps farmers grow food.
Name crops grown in Pakistan.
Link farm technology to what it does.
Sequence how a crop is grown with help from AI.
Know that farmers and AI work together.
Use data to make a farm decision.
Solve word problems about a smart farm.
Think about using AI wisely on a farm.
Learn key farm and technology words.
Design technology that helps farmers.

guide.what: Farmers in Pakistan grow wheat, rice, cotton, sugarcane, mangoes and much more. AI tools such as soil sensors, plant cameras, weather apps and smart tractors give farmers information to save water and spot problems early. The farmer still makes the decisions and cares for the land and animals.
steps: Talk about where your food comes from: which crops grow near you?
Look at a weather forecast together and ask how a farmer would use it.
Ask: what would a farmer do if the soil is dry and no rain is coming?
home: Grow a seed in a cup and be the 'sensor': check the soil each day and record dry or wet.
Visit a fruit or vegetable market and name where each crop grows.
guide.watch: Children may think robots do all the farm work. Remind them that farmers do the hard work and make the choices; AI is a helper.

title: Training a model (unplugged) Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 AI practice on training a model (unplugged), from "What Is a Model?" to "My Own Model". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a model learns from labelled examples.
Sequence the steps of training a model.
Label examples for a model.
Use a learned rule to classify, like a model.
Read a model's test score.
Choose good examples for training.
Solve word problems about training a model.
Learn key words about training a model.
Train a person like a model, without a computer.
Plan your own model.

guide.what: Training a model means showing it many labelled examples so it can find patterns, then testing it with new examples to see how well it learned. Good training data is varied, clear and labelled correctly. Children can do this unplugged by sorting cards and guessing secret rules.
steps: Play the secret rule game: sort objects into yes and no and let your child find the rule.
Ask: what examples would help the model learn better?
Count right answers out of 10 to talk about accuracy.
home: Make a set of fruit and vegetable cards and 'train' a younger child or toy.
Collect leaves from the garden and label them by shape.
guide.watch: Children sometimes think AI learns by itself from nothing. Stress that people collect and label the examples.

title: AI in games Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on ai in games, from "Game AI" to "Design a Game Character". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know how AI is used in video and board games.
Sequence how a game AI picks a move.
Spot where AI is used in games.
See how AI can learn a game from practice.
Learn key words about game AI.
Solve word problems with game scores.
Make healthy, safe choices with games.
Notice how some games are built to keep you playing.
Judge if game AI is fair.
Design rules for a game AI.

guide.what: Games use AI for computer opponents, for characters that chase or help, and to adjust levels. Some programs learned games like chess by playing themselves millions of times, keeping moves that won. Games can also be designed to keep children playing, so it helps to know the tricks and stay in charge of screen time.
steps: Play a board game together and talk about your strategy out loud.
Ask: how does the computer player choose its move?
Agree on game time limits and in-game buying rules as a family.
home: Invent a simple board game with an 'AI rule' for the computer player, such as 'always move toward the nearest coin'.
Keep a one-week log of game time and talk about it.
guide.watch: Talk about in-game purchases and chatting with strangers before they come up. Children should always ask before buying or chatting.

title: Ethics: who decides? Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 AI practice on ethics: who decides?, from "What Is Ethics?" to "My AI Rules". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that people decide how AI should be used.
Know who makes decisions about AI.
Learn five values for good AI.
Spot which value a case breaks.
Use steps to think through an AI decision.
Weigh good and bad points of an AI idea.
Use survey numbers about an AI decision.
Form and give your own view.
Learn key words about AI ethics.
Write your own AI ethics rules.

guide.what: AI does not decide its own rules: people do. Engineers, companies, governments, schools, families and users all make choices about how AI is built and used. Good AI is fair, private, safe, honest, and keeps people in charge. Children practise ethics by weighing good and bad points, thinking about who is affected and giving reasons for their views.
steps: Discuss a real AI idea, like face cameras in shops, and list good points and worries.
Ask: who should decide, and who should be asked?
Let your child disagree with you, as long as they give a reason.
home: Hold a family vote on a home tech rule after everyone gives a reason.
Make a poster of five rules for good AI.
guide.watch: There is often no single right answer in ethics. Praise good reasons and listening to others, not just the 'right' opinion.

words: what the AI is trained to do

title: Instructions for robots Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on instructions for robots, from "Robots Need Instructions" to "My Robot Steps". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a robot does exactly what its instructions say.
Read arrows as robot instructions.
Follow step instructions on a grid.
Put robot steps in the right order.
Tell clear instructions from unclear ones.
See what happens when a step is missing.
Solve word problems about robot steps.
Know common robot instruction words.
Act out instructions to learn how robots work.
Write your own robot instructions.

guide.what: Robots and computers follow instructions exactly, one step at a time and in order. They cannot guess what we mean. Children learn this by giving clear arrow steps (up, down, left, right), spotting missing steps and fixing mistakes. This is the first step of coding.
steps: Play 'Be the robot': your child gives you steps to walk to the door.
Follow a step exactly but silly, like a robot, so your child sees why clear steps matter.
Use the words forward, turn, stop and repeat.
home: Draw a grid with chalk outside and move a toy along arrow steps.
Write the steps for making a glass of lemonade together.
guide.watch: Children often skip small steps because people fill the gaps. Robots cannot, so praise your child when they remember a tiny step.

title: Learning from mistakes Practice
subject: AI
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 AI practice on learning from mistakes, from "Mistakes Help Us Learn" to "My Mistake Story". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that people and AI learn from mistakes.
Check if a guess is right.
Correct a wrong guess.
Know the steps of learning from a mistake.
Choose helpful ways to deal with a mistake.
See how feedback helps AI learn.
Solve word problems about trying again.
Know words that help after a mistake.
Know why we check answers from machines.
Reflect on learning from a mistake.

guide.what: AI learns by guessing, finding out if it was right or wrong, and trying again, many times over. People learn the same way. This topic helps children see mistakes as a normal part of learning, practise checking and fixing, and know that machines make mistakes too.
steps: Share a mistake you made and how you fixed it.
Use the words try, check, fix and try again.
When your child is upset by a mistake, say: that is how brains learn.
home: Play a guessing game: you say right or wrong, your child tries again.
Make a 'mistakes help me learn' poster for the bedroom.
guide.watch: Children can be very hard on themselves. Praise effort and trying again, not only getting it right.

title: Picture words and labels Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Nursery English practice on picture words and labels, from "Words Tell Us" to "My Labelled Picture". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a label is a word that names a picture.
Trace short picture words.
Write a label for a picture.
Hear the first sound of a picture word.
Choose the label that matches a picture.
Read labels on things at home.
Spot the same word again and again.
Label the parts of a face.
Count picture words.
Draw and label a picture.

guide.what: Picture words and labels: a label is a word next to a picture that names it. Children read short words like cat, dog, sun and bus, hear first sounds and label things at home.
steps: Point to a picture, then the word under it, and read it together.
Say the first sound of each label slowly.
Let your child point to the word while you read.
home: Stick paper labels on the door, window and bed.
Make picture cards with a word under each one.
guide.watch: Children may 'read' a label by guessing from the picture. Cover the picture sometimes and see if they can still read the word.

title: Adding with pictures Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Nursery Maths practice on adding with pictures, from "Putting Together" to "My Adding Picture". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that adding means putting groups together.
Add two small groups of pictures.
Add with fruit pictures.
Add one more to a number.
Add in picture stories.
Choose the total of two groups.
Draw groups to add.
Add in short number stories.
Match sums to answers.
Show an adding story in a picture.

guide.what: Adding with pictures: putting two small groups together and counting how many in all, up to 5. Children meet the + sign, add one more and solve picture stories.
steps: Use real things: 2 spoons and 1 more spoon.
Push the two groups together, then count them all.
Say the sum aloud: two and one more makes three.
home: Add sweets, buttons or toys at snack time.
Sing a counting song and add one more each verse.
guide.watch: Some children count each group but forget to count them all together. Move the groups into one pile, then count.

title: Water and keeping clean Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on water and keeping clean, from "We Need Water" to "I Keep Clean". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that we need water every day.
Name ways we use water.
Follow the steps to wash hands.
Know when to wash our hands.
Know the things that keep us clean.
Tell clean habits from dirty ones.
Learn to save water.
Match cleaning things to what they do.
Count in water stories.
Show a clean habit.

guide.what: Water and keeping clean: we need clean water to drink and wash, we wash hands with soap at the right times, brush teeth and bathe, and we save water by turning off the tap.
steps: Wash hands together and count to 20 while you rub.
Talk about when we wash: before eating, after the toilet.
Turn off the tap while brushing teeth.
home: Make soap bubbles together.
Water a plant and watch it over the week.
guide.watch: Children often rinse quickly without soap. Make soap and a slow count part of the routine every time.

title: سردی کے الفاظ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on winter words (سردی کے الفاظ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read simple winter words.
Trace winter words.
Name winter things.
Hear the first letter of a winter word.
Choose the word for a picture.
Tell winter things from summer things.
Match Urdu winter words to English.
Spot a word among other words.
Count in short winter stories.
Write a winter word and draw yourself.

guide.what: Winter words in Urdu: برف، کوٹ، ٹوپی، موزے، دستانے، چائے and آگ. Children read and trace the words, hear the first letter and sort winter and summer things.
steps: Name each warm thing in Urdu as your child puts it on.
Ask: کوٹ کا پہلا حرف کون سا ہے؟
Read the word cards with real things at home.
home: Make winter word cards and play a matching game.
Say a winter word and ask your child to point to the thing.
guide.watch: موزے and دستانے are long words for little ones. Clap the parts: مو-زے، دس-تا-نے.

title: Opposites Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of KG English practice on opposites, from "What Is an Opposite?" to "Draw Opposites". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that opposites are words that mean very different things.
Name opposites from pictures.
Find the opposite of a word.
Write pairs of opposite words.
Use opposites to describe pictures.
Use an opposite in a sentence.
Sort opposite pairs.
Find opposites in a short story.
Use maths with opposite words.
Draw and label a pair of opposites.

guide.what: Opposites are words that mean very different things: big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow, day and night, open and shut, full and empty.
steps: Say a word and ask your child for its opposite.
Act out opposites: stand up tall, then crouch down small.
Point out opposites in picture books.
home: Play the opposite game in the car: up? down!
Feel a hot cup and a cold glass and say the words.
guide.watch: Some words have more than one opposite: short can be the opposite of tall or of long. Accept both when they make sense.

title: Measuring with hands and feet Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of KG Maths practice on measuring with hands and feet, from "How Long Is It?" to "My Measuring". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that we can measure with our hands and feet.
Read a measure in hand spans.
Compare lengths.
Read a measure in foot steps.
Choose a good unit for measuring.
Follow the steps to measure with hand spans.
Find the longest and shortest.
Know that different hands give different answers.
Solve number stories about measuring.
Measure real things with hands and feet.

guide.what: Measuring length with hand spans and foot steps: counting how many spans or steps long something is, comparing longer and shorter, and seeing why different hands give different answers.
steps: Show your child how to stretch a hand span from thumb to little finger.
Measure the same table with your hand and your child's hand. Compare.
Walk heel to toe across a room and count the steps.
home: Measure toys with paper clips or blocks.
Make a list of things longer and shorter than your bed.
guide.watch: Children leave gaps between hand spans. Show them to start the next span exactly where the last one ended.

title: Places in our town Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on places in our town, from "Our Town" to "My Town". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a town has many useful places.
Name places in a town.
Match helpers to where they work.
Choose the right place for a job.
Link things to the places they belong.
Plan a trip across town.
Sort places to learn, to play and to get help.
Find places on a simple town map.
Use maths in town stories.
Draw and describe a favourite place.

guide.what: Places in our town: homes, school, hospital, mosque, post office, bank, station, shops and parks, who works there and what we do there, and finding them on a simple map.
steps: On a walk or drive, name each place you pass.
Ask: who works here? what do we do here?
Draw a simple map of your street together.
home: Play shop at home with a till and fruit.
Visit the post office and post a card to a grandparent.
guide.watch: Children may not know the difference between a clinic and a hospital, or a shop and a market. Use the words you see on real signs.

title: نظم: سردی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of KG Urdu practice on poem: winter (نظم: سردی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read and recite a short winter poem.
Learn the new words in the poem.
Find rhyming words in the poem.
Complete lines of the poem from memory.
Name things from the poem.
Answer questions about the poem.
Sort winter and summer things.
Put a winter day in order.
Solve short Urdu number stories.
Draw and write about winter.

guide.what: A short original Urdu poem about winter: cold wind, warm clothes, peanuts and gur in the sunshine and a soft quilt at night. Children recite it, learn new words, find rhyming words (آئی، لائی) and answer questions.
steps: Read the poem aloud with actions: shiver, put on a hat, sit in the sun.
Stop before a rhyming word and let your child say it.
Talk about the new words رضائی and گُڑ.
home: Eat peanuts in the sunshine and recite the poem together.
Make a winter picture and write one line of the poem under it.
guide.watch: Children may say رجائی for رضائی. Say the word slowly and point to ض.

title: Asking a grown-up online Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 ICT practice on asking a grown-up online, from "Ask First" to "My Ask Card". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that we ask a grown-up before we do new things online.
Follow three steps when unsure online.
Decide when to ask a grown-up.
Name trusted grown-ups.
Know what we keep private online.
Spot tricky pop-ups and buttons.
Choose the right action online.
Use polite words to ask for help.
Use maths in online stories.
Make a reminder to ask a grown-up online.

guide.what: Asking a grown-up online: stop, think and ask before clicking, downloading, paying or chatting; keeping private things private; and telling a trusted grown-up about pop-ups, strangers or anything upsetting.
steps: Sit with your child the first time they use a new app or game.
Agree a family rule: we ask before we download or pay.
Praise your child every time they come and ask.
home: Make an Ask Card together and stick it near the screen.
Look at a pop-up together and talk about why it is tricky.
guide.watch: Children may hide a mistake for fear of trouble. Stay calm and thank them for telling you, so they keep coming back.

title: Book review Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 English practice on book review, from "What Is a Book Review?" to "My Book Review". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a book review tells a reader.
Name the parts of a book used in a review.
Read a short story and pick out its main parts.
Find the characters, setting and problem of a story.
Use describing words to talk about books.
Tell facts about a book from opinions about it.
Match an opinion to a star rating.
Write a review without spoiling the ending.
Solve word problems about books and reading.
Write a short book review of your own.

guide.what: Writing a book review: the parts of a book (title, author, illustrator, cover, blurb), characters, setting and problem, describing words, fact and opinion, star ratings and not giving away the ending.
steps: Read a short story together and talk about who, where and what happened.
Ask: what did you like best and why?
Help your child give stars and explain the rating.
home: Keep a reading log with a star rating for every book.
Visit a library or bookshop and read the blurbs on the back.
guide.watch: Children often retell the whole story. Remind them a review gives a taste and their opinion, not every event.

title: Fractions of shapes and amounts Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on fractions of shapes and amounts, from "Equal Parts" to "Make Your Own Fractions". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a fraction means equal parts of a whole.
Name halves, thirds and quarters of shapes.
Read and write fraction words.
Find half of a number of objects.
Find a quarter and a third of a number.
Find fractions of real things.
Check whether a share is equal.
See that 2/4 is the same as 1/2.
Solve word problems with fractions.
Show fractions by colouring and in a story.

guide.what: Fractions of shapes and amounts: equal parts, halves, thirds and quarters of shapes, half, a quarter and a third of a number, fair sharing, and seeing that 2/4 is the same as 1/2.
steps: Cut a roti or sandwich into equal parts and name them.
Share sweets or beans into equal groups to find half or a quarter.
Always check: are the parts the same size?
home: Fold paper into halves and quarters and colour one part.
When sharing fruit, ask: what fraction did each person get?
guide.watch: Children may call any two pieces halves. Show that halves must be equal by putting one piece on top of the other.

title: Sound around us Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on sound around us, from "What Is Sound?" to "Make a String Telephone". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that sounds are made when things vibrate.
Feel and notice vibrations that make sounds.
Name sounds from everyday things.
Sort sounds as loud or soft.
Know that sounds can be high or low.
Know how instruments make sounds.
Know that sound travels through air, water and solids.
Know what an echo is and how to protect our ears.
Use maths with sound facts.
Plan a simple sound investigation.

guide.what: Sound: things vibrate to make sounds, sound travels through air, water and solids, loud and soft sounds, high and low pitch, musical instruments, echoes and caring for our ears.
steps: Hum with your hand on your throat to feel vibrations.
Go on a sound walk and list what you hear.
Tap a table with your ear on it and then off it.
home: Make a string telephone with two paper cups.
Fill glasses with different amounts of water and tap them to hear high and low notes.
guide.watch: Children often mix up loud and high. A high sound can be soft (a little bird) and a low sound can be loud (thunder).

title: Allama Iqbal's dream Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 History practice on allama iqbal's dream, from "Who Was Allama Iqbal?" to "My Dream". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know who Allama Muhammad Iqbal was.
Order the main events of Iqbal's life.
Remember key facts about Allama Iqbal.
Know about Iqbal's dream of a separate homeland.
Know why Iqbal is called the Poet of the East.
Link places to events in Iqbal's life.
Link Iqbal's ideas to good habits today.
Know how Pakistan remembers Iqbal.
Use maths with dates from Iqbal's life.
Share a dream for your country.

guide.what: Allama Muhammad Iqbal (1877 to 1938): born in Sialkot, poet in Urdu and Persian, studied in England and Germany, gave the 1930 Allahabad speech about a Muslim homeland, called Shair-e-Mashriq (Poet of the East), National Poet of Pakistan, buried in Lahore near the Badshahi Mosque. Iqbal Day is 9 November.
steps: Find Sialkot, Lahore and Allahabad on a map.
Talk about what a dream for the country means.
Ask: why did Iqbal like the shaheen?
home: Visit or look at pictures of Mazar-e-Iqbal in Lahore.
Make a timeline of Iqbal's life with five dates.
guide.watch: Children often think Iqbal made Pakistan himself. He shared the idea; Quaid-e-Azam and many others worked to make it real, after Iqbal had died.

title: Farming in Pakistan Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on farming in pakistan, from "A Farming Country" to "My Farm". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that farming is very important in Pakistan.
Name important crops of Pakistan.
Know that some crops grow in winter and some in summer.
Know how farms get water.
Order the steps of growing wheat.
Know how farm animals help us.
Read a simple farm map with directions.
Compare old and new ways of farming.
Use maths with farm facts.
Plan a farm using what you learned.

guide.what: Farming in Pakistan: main crops (wheat, rice, cotton, sugarcane, maize, mangoes), Rabi winter crops and Kharif summer crops, water from the Indus through dams, canals and tube wells, the steps from seed to roti, farm animals, and old and new ways of farming.
steps: Look at the food on your table and ask which crop it came from.
Find Punjab and Sindh on a map and trace the canals.
Talk about which crops grow in winter and which in summer.
home: Grow chickpeas or wheat seeds in a cup of soil.
Visit a vegetable market and name where each crop grows.
guide.watch: Children may think food comes from shops. Trace one food, like roti, back to the farmer and the field.

title: Caring for animals Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on caring for animals, from "Animals Need Care" to "My Animal Promise". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what animals need to stay healthy.
Know what some animals eat.
Tell kind actions from unkind ones.
Know people who care for animals.
Plan a daily pet care routine.
Tell pets from wild animals.
Know how to stay safe near animals.
Know how to help animals in cold weather.
Use maths with animal care.
Make a plan to be kind to animals.

guide.what: Caring for animals: what animals need (food, water, shelter and care), what they eat, kind and unkind actions, people who help animals (vets, zookeepers, shelters, farmers), a daily pet routine, pets and wild animals, staying safe and helping animals in winter.
steps: Talk about what a pet needs every day.
Show your child how to approach an animal gently.
Remind them to wash hands after touching animals.
home: Put out a bowl of water and some grain for birds on the roof.
Make a pet care chart with a tick for each job.
guide.watch: Children may want to pick up or hug every animal they see. Teach them to ask a grown-up and to let animals come to them.

title: سردی کی نظم کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on poem about winter (سردی کی نظم), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read and recite a winter poem.
Learn the meanings of new words from the poem.
Find rhyming words in the poem.
Complete lines of the poem.
Answer questions about the poem.
Name winter things in Urdu.
Sort words into winter and summer.
Understand the meaning of lines from the poem.
Read and solve Urdu number stories.
Write two rhyming lines about winter.

guide.what: An original Urdu poem about a winter morning (سردی کی صبح): reading and reciting, new words (دھند، شبنم، اونی، دستانے)، rhyming words (ہم قافیہ), the meaning of each line, winter things in Urdu and writing two rhyming lines.
steps: Read the poem aloud together with expression.
Clap the rhythm of each line.
Ask your child to find words that rhyme.
home: Look for dew on leaves on a winter morning and say the word شبنم.
Make up a new rhyming line about your family in winter.
guide.watch: Children may think rhyming words must look the same. Rhyming is about the sound at the end, like شال and لال.

words: کہرا، جس میں کچھ نظر نہ آئے
صبح پتوں پر پانی کی بوندیں

title: Passwords and privacy Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 ICT practice on passwords and privacy, from "What Is a Password?" to "My Safety Rules". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a password is for.
Tell strong passwords from weak ones.
Know which information is private.
Learn habits that keep devices safe.
Choose safe actions online.
Build a strong password with a recipe.
Spot messages that try to steal passwords.
Decide who can know your password.
Use maths with passwords.
Make a set of personal online safety rules.

guide.what: Passwords and privacy: what a password is, strong and weak passwords, private information (address, phone number, password), habits like locking and logging out, spotting tricks that ask for passwords, and who may know your password.
steps: Make a family password together using three random words.
Talk about which information is private.
Agree that your child tells you about any strange message.
home: Play a game: you say a piece of information, your child says private or fine to share.
Make a lock and key poster for the computer corner.
guide.watch: Children may think a best friend can know their password. Explain that friends fall out and passwords stay between child and parent.

title: Poetry: rhyme and rhythm Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 English practice on poetry: rhyme and rhythm, from "What Makes a Poem?" to "Write Your Own Poem". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the main features of a poem.
Identify words that rhyme.
Spot a rhyme pattern (AABB and ABAB).
Complete couplets with rhyming words.
Know that rhythm is the beat of a poem.
Recognise onomatopoeia in poems.
Recognise repetition and alliteration.
Understand and respond to a poem.
Check whether word pairs rhyme.
Write a short rhyming poem.

guide.what: Poetry at Grade 4 level: lines and verses, rhyming words, rhyme patterns (AABB and ABAB), finishing couplets, rhythm and syllable beats, onomatopoeia, repetition, alliteration, reading and responding to a poem, and writing a four-line rhyming poem.
steps: Read a short poem aloud together and clap the beat.
Play a rhyming game in the car: one person says a word, the next says a rhyme.
Point out sound words in comics and story books: bang, splash, whoosh.
home: Learn a short English poem by heart and say it to the family.
Make up a funny alliteration about each family member, like Dancing Dada.
guide.watch: Children often think words must be spelt the same to rhyme. Rhyme is about sound, so blue and shoe rhyme. They may also force a rhyme that makes no sense; meaning comes first.

title: Area and perimeter Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on area and perimeter, from "What Is Perimeter?" to "Design a Garden". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that perimeter is the distance around a shape.
Find the perimeter of rectangles and squares.
Know that area is the space a shape covers.
Find the area of a rectangle by multiplying.
Decide whether a job needs area or perimeter.
Use area and perimeter in real life.
Work backwards from area or perimeter.
Know that shapes with the same area can have different perimeters.
Solve problems with area and perimeter.
Use area and perimeter to design a space.

guide.what: Area and perimeter: perimeter as the distance around a shape, adding sides of rectangles and squares, area as the space inside a shape in square units, area = length × width, choosing area or perimeter for real jobs, finding a missing side, and shapes with the same area but different perimeters.
steps: Walk around a room counting steps to feel the perimeter, then count floor tiles to see the area.
Measure a book, a table and a photo frame with a ruler and work out their perimeters.
Use squared paper to draw rectangles and count the squares.
home: Measure your bedroom with a tape and work out its area.
Plan a small vegetable patch and work out how much fence it would need.
guide.watch: Children often mix up area and perimeter. Remind them: perimeter goes around the edge (a fence), area covers the inside (a carpet). They also forget to add all four sides of a rectangle.

title: Sound and vibration Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on sound and vibration, from "Sound Is a Vibration" to "Make a Musical Instrument". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that sounds are made when things vibrate.
Identify the vibrating part of sound makers.
Know that sound travels through solids, liquids and gases.
Order how the ear hears a sound.
Know what pitch is.
Know what makes a sound loud or soft.
Explain how a string telephone works.
Know how to look after our hearing.
Use maths with sound.
Plan an instrument that can change pitch.

guide.what: Sound and vibration: sounds are made by vibrations, identifying what vibrates in instruments and voices, sound travelling through solids, liquids and gases (and not in space), how the ear and eardrum work, pitch (high and low), volume (loud and soft), a string telephone, caring for our hearing, and the speed of sound and thunder.
steps: Put your hand on your throat and hum to feel the vibration.
Stretch a rubber band and pluck it, then stretch it tighter and listen for a higher note.
Count the seconds between lightning and thunder in a storm.
home: Make a string telephone with two paper cups and a long string.
Fill glass bottles with different amounts of water and blow across the tops to make a tune.
guide.watch: Children often think sound only travels through air. It travels through water and solids too, and even faster through solids. They may also mix up pitch (high or low) with volume (loud or soft).

title: Ancient Persia Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 History practice on ancient persia, from "Where Was Ancient Persia?" to "Be a Historian". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know where and when Ancient Persia was.
Know about the first great Persian king.
Know about Darius the Great and his palace city.
Know how the Persians ran their empire.
Know about the Royal Road and the first postal riders.
Know Persian inventions and ideas.
Know the link between Persia and Pakistan.
Order the main events of Ancient Persia.
Count years BCE.
Explain why Ancient Persia matters.

guide.what: Ancient Persia: where and when the Persian empire was, Cyrus the Great and his fair rule, Darius the Great and Persepolis, satrapies and gold darics, the Royal Road and its relay riders, Persian ideas (qanats, gardens, polo), the link with the Indus and the Persian words in Urdu, and Alexander's conquest in 330 BCE.
steps: Find Iran next to Pakistan on a map and trace a route from Persepolis to the River Indus.
Make a list of Urdu words that come from Persian.
Look at pictures of Persepolis online together.
home: Play a relay race in the garden to act out the Royal Road riders.
Ask grandparents if they know any Persian poetry, such as lines by Saadi or Iqbal.
guide.watch: Children often find BCE dates confusing because the numbers get smaller as time moves forward. A simple number line from 600 BCE to today helps.

title: Pollution and the environment Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on pollution and the environment, from "What Is Pollution?" to "My Clean Earth Pledge". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what pollution is.
Know air, water, land and noise pollution.
Know about smog in Pakistan.
Read a simple air quality scale.
Know how pollution harms living things.
Know the three Rs.
Judge which actions help the environment.
Order the steps of a clean-up plan.
Use maths with pollution.
Plan actions to reduce pollution.

guide.what: Pollution and the environment: what the environment and pollution are, air, water, land and noise pollution, winter smog in Pakistan's cities, the Air Quality Index, how pollution harms people, animals and plants, reduce, reuse and recycle, judging helpful and harmful actions, and planning a clean-up.
steps: Check the AQI for your city on a weather app together and talk about what the number means.
Count the plastic bags in your kitchen and find ways to use fewer.
Set up two bins at home: one for rubbish and one for recycling.
home: Take a cloth bag on the next shopping trip.
Join or plan a small litter pick-up in your street or park with gloves and a grown-up.
guide.watch: Children may think pollution only means litter. Air and noise pollution are harder to see but just as harmful. They may also think recycling alone solves the problem: reducing comes first.

title: Volunteering Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on volunteering, from "What Is Volunteering?" to "My Volunteer Plan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a volunteer is.
Know different ways people volunteer.
Know about a great Pakistani volunteer.
Know how volunteering helps others and ourselves.
Think about how your skills can help others.
Know how volunteers help in emergencies.
Know how children can help safely.
Order the steps of a volunteering project.
Use maths with volunteering.
Plan a small volunteering project.

guide.what: Volunteering: what a volunteer is, different ways to help (reading, planting, animal shelters, food boxes), Abdul Sattar Edhi and the Edhi Foundation, why volunteering helps everyone, matching skills to needs, volunteers in the 2022 floods, helping safely, and planning a small project.
steps: Talk about people you know who help others without being paid.
Choose a small family project: sorting old toys and books to give away.
Read about Abdul Sattar Edhi together.
home: Make a water bowl for birds or street cats in summer.
Collect old school books in good condition for a younger cousin or a school in need.
guide.watch: Children sometimes think only big acts count as volunteering. Small, regular help counts too. Remind them to always help with a grown-up they know.

title: نظم کا مطالعہ کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on poem study (نظم کا مطالعہ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know the parts of an Urdu poem.
Read a poem and answer questions.
Know what qafia (rhyme) is.
Know what radeef is.
Learn the meanings of words in the poem.
Complete lines of the poem from memory.
Find the main idea of a poem.
Tell poetry from prose.
Write rhyming words.
Write a couplet with a rhyme.

guide.what: Poem study in Urdu (نظم کا مطالعہ): نظم، شاعر، مصرع، شعر اور عنوان; reading an original poem صبح کا منظر and answering questions; قافیہ (rhyming words) and ردیف (the repeated word); word meanings; completing lines; the مرکزی خیال (main idea); telling نظم from نثر; and writing a couplet.
steps: Read the poem aloud together with expression, then let your child read it to you.
Play a qafia game: say an Urdu word and take turns finding words that rhyme.
Talk about the main idea of any Urdu poem in your child's course book.
home: Learn صبح کا منظر by heart and say it at breakfast.
Write a family couplet together about something everyone loves.
guide.watch: Children often mix up qafia and radeef. The qafia changes but sounds alike (جہان، آسمان). The radeef is the same word repeated after it (ہے).

title: Online research and checking sources Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 ICT practice on online research and checking sources, from "What Is Research?" to "My Research Project". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what online research is.
Choose good keywords for a search.
Understand a page of search results.
Ask questions to check a website.
Check facts using more than one source.
Spot clues that something online may be fake.
Know not to copy and to say where facts came from.
Order the steps of a research project.
Know what to do when something goes wrong online.
Plan and carry out simple online research.

guide.what: Online research and checking sources: what research is, using a search engine, choosing keywords, reading search results and spotting adverts, asking who wrote a page and when, checking facts on two or three sources, clues that something may be fake, writing in your own words and listing sources, and staying safe while searching.
steps: Search for an answer together and talk about which result looks most trustworthy and why.
Practise turning a question into keywords: What do camels eat? becomes camels food.
Show your child the Ad or Sponsored label on search results.
home: Pick a family question at dinner and find the answer in a book and on two websites.
Look at a surprising picture or message forwarded on a family group and check together whether it is true.
guide.watch: Children often trust the first result or anything that looks official. They may also copy whole sentences. Teach them to check two or three sources and write notes in their own words.

title: Rhymes and songs about winter Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Nursery English practice on rhymes and songs about winter, from "Words That Rhyme" to "My Winter Rhyme". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Hear when two words rhyme.
Join in with a short winter rhyme.
Find a word that rhymes with a picture.
Trace words that rhyme.
Remember words from a winter song.
Spot words that rhyme.
Hear a word that does not rhyme.
Act out a winter song in order.
Count in short winter rhymes.
Show a rhyme in a picture.

guide.what: Rhymes and songs about winter: words that rhyme sound the same at the end (cat and hat, snow and go). Children join in with short original winter rhymes, find rhyming words and spot the odd one out.
steps: Say the rhymes with big actions: shiver, put on a hat, sip tea.
Stop before the last word of a line and let your child say it.
Say two words and ask: do they rhyme?
home: Make up a silly rhyme with your child's name.
Sing the Getting Ready Song while dressing on a cold morning.
guide.watch: Children often think words rhyme if they start the same (cat and cup). Stress the end sound: c-AT, h-AT.

title: Counting to 20 with objects Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Nursery Maths practice on counting to 20 with objects, from "Up to Twenty" to "My Collection". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the numbers 16 to 20.
Count groups of 16 to 20.
Write the numbers 16, 17 and 18.
Write the numbers 19 and 20.
Say and write the numbers 1 to 20 in order.
Match a group to its number.
Count on from ten.
Find one more and one less than a number to 20.
Solve number stories to 20.
Count a collection of 20 objects.

guide.what: Counting to 20 with real objects: the numbers 16 to 20, counting on from ten, one more and one less, and solving short number stories.
steps: Touch or move each object as you count it.
Line up 10 things first, then count on: eleven, twelve.
Count stairs, spoons or shoes up to 20.
home: Count 20 beans into a cup at snack time.
Play a game: you say a number, your child says one more.
guide.watch: Children may skip or count an object twice when there are many. Move each object to a new pile as you count it.

title: Sounds around us Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on sounds around us, from "We Hear Sounds" to "My Loud Sound". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that we hear sounds with our ears.
Match animals to the sounds they make.
Tell loud sounds from quiet sounds.
Name sounds we hear at home.
Sort sounds we hear at home and outside.
Know that some sounds keep us safe.
Name things that make music.
Sort animal sounds and machine sounds.
Count in sound stories.
Show loud and quiet sounds.

guide.what: Sounds around us: we hear with our ears; animals, machines and music make sounds; some sounds are loud and some are quiet; and some sounds, like a siren or a bell, help keep us safe.
steps: Sit quietly for one minute and name every sound you hear.
Make animal sounds together and guess the animal.
Clap loudly, then softly.
home: Make a shaker with rice in a bottle.
Go on a sound walk and count the sounds you hear.
guide.watch: Very loud sounds can hurt our ears. Teach children to cover their ears for loud noises and never to shout into someone's ear.

title: ننھی نظمیں: بارش اور دھوپ کی مشق
en: Little poems: rain and sun practice
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on little poems: rain and sun (ننھی نظمیں: بارش اور دھوپ), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Join in with a short rain poem.
Name rain words.
Trace rain words.
Join in with a short sun poem.
Trace sun words.
Find rhyming words in the poems.
Sort rain things and sun things.
Match Urdu words to English.
Count in short rain and sun stories.
Draw rain or sun and trace a word.

guide.what: Two short original Urdu poems for little ones, one about rain (بادل، بارش، بوندیں) and one about the morning sun (سورج، دھوپ، سویرا). Children join in, trace the new words, hear rhyming words and sort rain things and sun things.
steps: Say the poems with actions: tap fingers for ٹپ ٹپ, stretch arms wide for the sun.
Stop before the last word and let your child say it.
Point to the sky and name بادل and سورج.
home: Look out of the window each morning and ask: آج بارش ہے یا دھوپ؟
Draw a rain and sun picture and label it in Urdu.
guide.watch: Children may mix up بادل and بارش. Show that the cloud comes first and the rain falls from it.

title: Reading short stories Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of KG English practice on reading short stories, from "What Is a Story?" to "My Favourite Story". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a story has a beginning, a middle and an end.
Read a short story and answer questions.
Find the character, place and problem in a story.
Answer questions about a story.
Put the parts of a story in order.
Read words from the stories.
Match questions to answers about a story.
Tell how characters feel in a story.
Use maths with stories.
Draw and tell about a story.

guide.what: Reading short stories: a story has characters, a beginning, a middle and an end. Children read three short stories, answer questions, find who and where, put events in order and talk about how characters feel.
steps: Read each story aloud together, then let your child read it.
Ask: who is in the story? where are they? what went wrong?
Ask your child to retell the story with first, next, last.
home: Read a bedtime story and ask one question at the end.
Act out The Lost Shoe with a real shoe and a toy.
guide.watch: Children may guess answers from the pictures. Ask them to point to the words in the story that give the answer.

title: Halves Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of KG Maths practice on halves, from "What Is Half?" to "Draw the Halves". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that a half is one of two equal parts.
Recognise one half of a shape.
Tell equal parts from parts that are not equal.
Find half of a small group by sharing.
Find half of food at home.
Share a group into 2 equal halves.
Follow the steps to cut something in half.
Choose the half of a number.
Solve number stories about halves.
Split shapes into halves.

guide.what: Halves: a half is one of two equal parts, two halves make a whole, and to find half of a group we share it into two equal groups (half of 6 is 3).
steps: Cut fruit or roti into two halves and check they are the same size.
Share sweets into 2 equal groups: one for you, one for me.
Fold paper in half and open it to see the two halves.
home: Share snacks fairly with a sibling.
Fold a napkin in half at dinner time.
guide.watch: Children call any two pieces halves. Hold the pieces side by side: if one is bigger, they are not halves.

title: Winter animals and birds Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 10 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on winter animals and birds, from "Keeping Warm" to "My Winter Animal". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that animals have ways to stay warm in winter.
Know that some animals sleep all winter.
Know that some birds fly far away in winter.
Name animals that live in snowy places.
Match animals to their winter coats.
Know that some animals store food for winter.
Sort animals by what they do in winter.
Learn to help birds in cold weather.
Use maths in winter animal stories.
Draw and describe a winter animal.

guide.what: Winter animals and birds: how animals keep warm (fur, wool, feathers, fat), animals that sleep all winter (hibernation), birds that fly to warm places such as the lakes of Pakistan, and animals that store food.
steps: Look at birds in the garden and talk about how they puff up in the cold.
Ask: how does a sheep keep warm? how do we keep warm?
Look at pictures of snow leopards and markhor from the northern mountains.
home: Put out a small bowl of water and some grain for birds.
Visit a lake or park in winter and count the ducks.
guide.watch: Children may think animals sleeping in winter are ill or dead. Explain that hibernation is a long, deep rest and they wake up in spring.

title: مختصر کہانی اور سوالات کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of KG Urdu practice on short story with questions (مختصر کہانی اور سوالات), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a short Urdu story.
Learn the new words in the story.
Find words in the story.
Say if a sentence matches the story.
Put the story in order.
Name things from the story.
Tell how a character feels.
Read a second short story.
Solve short Urdu number stories.
Draw and write about a story.

guide.what: A short original Urdu story about Ali and his parrot Mithu, plus a second tiny story about a cat. Children read, learn new words (طوطا، پنجرہ، پیڑ، اداس), answer questions, say true or false, put events in order and talk about feelings.
steps: Read the story aloud first, then read it together line by line.
Ask the questions out loud before your child circles the answer.
Ask: علی کب اداس ہوا؟ کب خوش ہوا؟
home: Retell the story with a toy bird.
Make up a new ending: what if Mithu flew to the roof?
guide.watch: Children may answer from memory instead of the text. Ask them to find and point to the line in the story.

title: Coding with arrows Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 1 ICT practice on coding with arrows, from "What Is Code?" to "My Robot Game". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that code is a set of instructions a computer or robot follows.
Name the four direction arrows.
Follow arrow instructions on a grid.
Write code to reach a place on a grid.
Read a short program in order.
Know that a bug is a mistake in code.
Use repeat to make code shorter.
Know the words we use when coding.
Use maths with robot code.
Plan a robot path and write its code.

guide.what: Coding with arrows: code is a list of instructions that a robot follows exactly. Children name up, down, left and right arrows, follow and write arrow code on a grid, find and fix bugs, and use repeat to make code shorter.
steps: Play robot: your child gives you arrow instructions to walk across the room.
Draw a 3 by 3 grid on paper and move a coin with arrow cards.
When the coin ends up in the wrong place, look for the bug together.
home: Make arrow cards and build a path to a toy on the floor.
Try a free children's coding app with a grown-up.
guide.watch: Left and right are often mixed up. Put a small sticker on your child's right hand while playing.

title: Poems about winter Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 English practice on poems about winter, from "What Makes a Poem?" to "My Winter Poem". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the main features of a poem.
Read a poem and find details in it.
Find and make rhyming pairs.
Use the five senses to describe winter.
Choose strong adjectives for a poem.
Use similes to describe winter.
Count syllables to feel the rhythm of a line.
Read and understand an acrostic poem.
Use maths with poems.
Write a short winter poem of your own.

guide.what: Winter poems: what makes a poem (lines, verses, rhyme, rhythm), reading an original winter poem, rhyming pairs, using the five senses, describing words, similes, counting beats, acrostic poems and writing a winter poem.
steps: Read the poem aloud together and clap the rhythm.
Ask: what can you see, hear and feel in the poem?
Help your child find rhyming words.
home: Write an acrostic for your child's name or for WINTER.
Go outside on a winter morning and collect describing words.
guide.watch: Children may think every poem must rhyme. Many good poems do not; rhythm and strong pictures matter too.

title: Telling time to 5 minutes Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on telling time to 5 minutes, from "Counting in Fives" to "Draw the Hands". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that the minute hand moves 5 minutes from one number to the next.
Read times to 5 minutes past the hour.
Read times to 5 minutes on any clock.
Say times as minutes past or minutes to the hour.
Match digital times with time in words.
Read and write times for daily activities.
Work out how many minutes pass between two times.
Find the time 5, 10 or 30 minutes later or earlier.
Solve word problems about time.
Show times to 5 minutes by drawing clock hands.

guide.what: Telling the time to 5 minutes: counting in fives round the clock, reading times past and to the hour, matching digital times and words, finding how long something takes, and times before and after.
steps: Count in fives round a real clock with your finger.
Ask the time often during the day and let your child read it.
Use past for the right side of the clock and to for the left side.
home: Make a paper plate clock and set times for each other.
Time a short job, like brushing teeth, and count how many minutes it took.
guide.watch: Children often read the hour hand wrongly near the next hour. At 6:50 the hour hand is almost at 7, but it is still six fifty, ten to seven.

title: Weather and seasons Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on weather and seasons, from "What Is Weather?" to "My Weather Diary". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what weather is and how it changes.
Name different kinds of weather.
Name the seasons and their order.
Match things to the season they belong to.
Know simple weather tools.
Read temperatures and describe them.
Choose clothes and things for each kind of weather.
Read information from a weather chart.
Use maths with weather facts.
Observe and record the weather each day.

guide.what: Weather and seasons: what weather is, weather words, the four seasons and the monsoon in Pakistan, things for each season, weather tools, reading temperatures, dressing for the weather and reading a weather chart.
steps: Look out of the window each morning and name the weather.
Read the temperature on a phone or the news together.
Talk about what you wear in each season.
home: Make a rain gauge from a plastic bottle and a ruler.
Keep a weather diary on the fridge for a week.
guide.watch: Children may say it is winter whenever it rains. Explain that the season depends on the time of year, and weather is just today.

title: How we learn about the past Practice

subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 History practice on how we learn about the past, from "Clues from the Past" to "My Family History". An answer key for every page is at the back.

Name different kinds of historical sources.
Know what an artefact is and what it can tell us.
Know how archaeologists dig for the past.
Use artefacts to learn about an ancient city.
Compare objects from the past and today.
Sort old sources from new things.
Put events in order on a timeline.
Use maths with dates.
Collect a memory as a history source.
