guide.what: How we learn about the past: history and sources, kinds of sources (objects, writing, photos, buildings, memories), artefacts, how archaeologists work, clues from Mohenjo-daro, old and new things, and timelines.
steps: Look at old family photos together and ask: what is different?
Talk to grandparents about their childhood.
Ask: what does this old object tell us?
home: Make a family timeline with five important dates.
Visit a museum, such as the Lahore Museum, or look at its pictures online.
guide.watch: Children may think everything old is from the same time. Use a timeline to show that Mohenjo-daro is far older than the Mughals.

title: Winter around the world Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on winter around the world, from "Not the Same Everywhere" to "Postcard from Winter". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that winter comes at different times in different places.
Name the two halves of the Earth and the line between them.
Read a simple map with compass directions.
Know what winter is like in some places.
Compare December weather north and south of the Equator.
Know how people around the world cope with cold.
Name winter activities around the world.
Know how animals survive the winter.
Use maths with temperatures and travel.
Describe winter in another place.

guide.what: Winter around the world: the tilted Earth, the Equator, winter in the north while the south has summer, winter places (the Arctic, Canada, Russia, Murree, Antarctica), keeping warm, winter sports and how animals cope with cold.
steps: Use a globe and a torch to show how the Earth tilts.
Find the Equator, Pakistan and Australia on a map.
Ask: what is the weather like in Australia today?
home: Check the weather in three cities around the world on a phone.
Make a list of things your family does to keep warm.
guide.watch: Children often think everyone has winter in December. Show that south of the Equator it is summer then.

title: Being a good neighbour Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on being a good neighbour, from "Who Are Neighbours?" to "My Neighbour Plan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know who our neighbours are.
Name kind things neighbours do.
Tell good neighbour habits from bad ones.
Know ways to help neighbours.
Choose respectful ways to behave with neighbours.
Plan a way to work together as neighbours.
Link problems with kind solutions.
Know that countries have neighbours too.
Use maths in neighbourhood stories.
Make a plan to help your neighbours.

guide.what: Being a good neighbour: who neighbours are, kind actions (sharing, greeting, helping, visiting), good and bad habits, helping when someone is sick, new or old, respect and quiet, working together on a clean-up, and countries as neighbours too.
steps: Talk about the neighbours on your street and their names.
Let your child help send food to a neighbour.
Ask: how would you feel if a neighbour was noisy at night?
home: Make a welcome card for a new family on your street.
Plant a tree or flowers by the gate with a neighbour.
guide.watch: Children may think being a good neighbour is only about sharing food. Being quiet, tidy and respectful matters just as much.

title: کہانی اور سوالات کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on story with questions (کہانی اور سوالات), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a short story and check facts from it.
Learn the meanings of new words from the story.
Answer who, what and where questions about the story.
Put the events of the story in order.
Name the characters and things in the story.
Match words from the story with their opposites.
Understand how a character feels.
Sort good and careless habits.
Read and solve Urdu number stories.
Write the lesson of the story and draw a scene.

guide.what: An original Urdu story (گم شدہ بستہ) about Hamza, who leaves his school bag in the van. Your child reads the story, learns new words, answers questions, puts events in order, names characters, finds opposites, talks about feelings and good habits, and writes the lesson of the story.
steps: Read the story aloud together, then let your child read it.
Ask who, what, where and when questions in Urdu.
Talk about how Hamza felt and why.
home: Ask your child to retell the story in their own words.
Write your child's name on their bag and books together.
guide.watch: Children may answer with one word. Encourage a full sentence, for example: حمزہ وین میں اسکول جاتا ہے۔

title: Using a tablet camera safely Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 2 ICT practice on using a tablet camera safely, from "The Tablet Camera" to "My Photo Rules". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what a tablet camera can do.
Name the parts and features of a camera app.
Know to ask before taking photos of people.
Choose safe ways to use a camera.
Follow steps to take a clear photo.
Spot photos that show private details.
Decide who should see the photos we take.
Look after a tablet and its camera.
Use maths with photos and videos.
Make personal rules for using a camera safely.

guide.what: Using a tablet camera safely: photos and videos, camera words (lens, flash, gallery, zoom, delete), asking before photographing people, safe and unsafe photos, steps for a clear photo, private details in photos, who can see shared photos and caring for the tablet.
steps: Take photos together and talk about what makes a good one.
Practise asking: may I take your photo?
Look at a photo together and check for private details before sharing.
home: Go on a photo walk in the garden and take five nature photos.
Make a small family album of your child's best photos.
guide.watch: Children may not notice private details in the background of a photo, like a school badge or house number. Check photos together before they are shared.

title: Reading comprehension: non-fiction Practice
subject: English
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 English practice on reading comprehension: non-fiction, from "Fiction or Non-fiction?" to "Make a Fact File". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell fiction from non-fiction.
Know the features of non-fiction texts.
Find facts in a non-fiction text.
Find the main idea and supporting details.
Use a contents page to find information.
Match headings to paragraphs.
Use a glossary to learn topic words.
Find and use facts in a table.
Retrieve facts and make inferences.
Write a short non-fiction fact file.

guide.what: Reading non-fiction at Grade 4 level: fiction and non-fiction, features (contents, headings, captions, diagrams, glossary, index), finding facts in a text about the Indus river dolphin, main idea and details, using a contents page, matching headings, glossary words, reading a table, retrieving and inferring from a text about the Khewra Salt Mine, and writing a fact file.
steps: Pick a non-fiction book at home or in a library and point out its contents page, headings and captions together.
Read a short news report together and ask: what is it mostly about?
Ask why questions whose answers are not written in the text, so your child has to think.
home: Visit a museum, zoo or the Khewra Salt Mine and make a fact file afterwards.
Make a family glossary of five new words learned this week.
guide.watch: Children often copy whole sentences instead of finding the exact fact asked for. They may also look only for answers written word for word; inference questions need them to think about clues.

title: Roman numerals Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on roman numerals, from "Numbers from Rome" to "My Roman Numerals". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the main Roman numeral letters.
Read numerals made by adding.
Read numerals made by subtracting.
Know the rules for writing Roman numerals.
Change numbers into Roman numerals.
Read Roman numerals in real life.
Compare Roman numerals.
Find and fix mistakes in Roman numerals.
Solve problems with Roman numerals.
Use Roman numerals for real numbers.

guide.what: Roman numerals: the letters I, V, X, L and C, adding letters (VI, XV), taking away (IV, IX, XL, XC), the rules for writing them, changing numbers to Roman numerals up to 100, Roman numerals on clocks, books and buildings, comparing them, fixing mistakes, and word problems.
steps: Look for Roman numerals on clocks, watches, book chapters and buildings when you are out.
Write the family's ages in Roman numerals on a chart.
Make number cards for I, V, X, L and C and build numbers together.
home: Make a paper clock face with Roman numerals and use it to tell the time.
Write a secret message for a sibling where page and line numbers are in Roman numerals.
guide.watch: Children often forget that a smaller letter before a bigger one means take away, so they read IV as 6. They may also write IIII or XXXX: remind them of the three-in-a-row rule.

title: Earth and the Moon Practice
subject: Science
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on earth and the moon, from "Our Planet Earth" to "My Moon Diary". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know how Earth moves.
Explain day and night.
Know that the Moon reflects light from the Sun.
Know key facts about the Moon.
Name the phases of the Moon.
Compare Earth and the Moon.
Know about the first Moon landing.
Know that gravity is weaker on the Moon.
Use maths with Earth and the Moon.
Observe and record the Moon's phases.

guide.what: Earth and the Moon: Earth as a spinning planet, rotation and day and night, Earth's orbit and the year, the Sun gives light while the Moon reflects it, facts about the Moon and its craters, the phases of the Moon, comparing Earth and the Moon, the 1969 Moon landing, gravity on the Moon, and space maths.
steps: Use a torch and a ball in a dark room to show day and night: the torch is the Sun.
Look at the Moon together each evening and talk about its shape.
Talk about the new moon and how it is looked for at the start of each lunar month.
home: Keep a Moon diary for two weeks and draw each phase.
Make Moon craters by dropping small stones into a tray of flour.
guide.watch: Children often think the Moon makes its own light, or that the Sun moves around Earth. They may think the Moon's phases are caused by Earth's shadow; they are caused by how much of the sunlit side we can see.

title: Explorers and maps Practice
subject: History
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 History practice on explorers and maps, from "Who Are Explorers?" to "Be an Explorer". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what explorers do.
Know about the great traveller Ibn Battuta.
Know about Al-Idrisi, a great mapmaker.
Know some explorers from around the world.
Know the tools explorers used.
Compare old and modern maps.
Know why explorers looked for sea routes.
Order famous journeys on a timeline.
Count years between dates.
Plan a journey and draw a simple map.

guide.what: Explorers and maps: who explorers are, Ibn Battuta and the Rihla, Al-Idrisi's world map of 1154, famous explorers from around the world (Marco Polo, Zheng He, Vasco da Gama, Columbus), tools for the journey (compass, stars, sails, hourglass), old and new maps, the spice routes, a timeline of journeys, and timeline maths.
steps: Find Morocco, Delhi and China on a world map and trace Ibn Battuta's route with a finger.
Look at a map app and an old map picture online together and spot the differences.
Talk about a family journey: how did you find the way?
home: Use a real compass or a phone compass to find north in your home or garden.
Draw a treasure map of your house with a key and hide a small surprise.
guide.watch: Children may think explorers found empty lands. Remind them that people already lived in most places, and that many explorers relied on local guides and sailors.

title: Reading atlases Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on reading atlases, from "What Is an Atlas?" to "My Atlas Quest". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what an atlas is.
Know the parts of a map.
Use eight compass directions.
Name continents and oceans.
Know the equator and the poles.
Find places using grid references.
Know physical and political maps.
Use a map scale to work out distances.
Use an atlas index to find places.
Find and describe places in an atlas.

guide.what: Reading atlases: what an atlas is, parts of a map (title, key, scale, compass rose, grid, index), eight compass points, continents and oceans, the equator, poles, latitude and longitude, grid references, physical and political maps, using a scale, and using an atlas index.
steps: Look through an atlas together and find Pakistan, its neighbours and the oceans.
Play a direction game: 'The kitchen is north-east of the lounge. True or false?'
Use a map app and zoom out until you see the whole continent.
home: Draw a map of your street with a grid and give each house a grid reference.
Pick a country each week and find it in the atlas index.
guide.watch: Children often give the number before the letter in grid references; remind them: along the corridor, then up the stairs. They may also mix up north-east and north-west.

words: tells you what the map shows

title: Global citizens Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on global citizens, from "What Is a Global Citizen?" to "My Global Citizen Pledge". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what it means to be a global citizen.
Know how countries are linked by trade.
Know what the United Nations does.
Know some rights every child has.
Know some of the world's global goals.
Learn greetings from around the world.
Show respect for other cultures.
Plan how to act as a global citizen.
Use maths with global facts.
Plan actions as a global citizen.

guide.what: Global citizens: what a global citizen is, how countries are linked by trade (Sialkot footballs, basmati rice, Kenyan tea), the United Nations and UNICEF, the rights of the child, the 17 Global Goals, greetings from around the world, respecting cultures, planning small actions, and world maths.
steps: Look at labels on food and clothes at home and find where they were made on a map.
Talk about a family friend or relative who lives in another country.
Learn to say hello in two new languages together.
home: Choose one Global Goal as a family and do one thing for it this week.
Cook or try a dish from another country and find that country in an atlas.
guide.watch: Children sometimes think world problems are too big for them. Small actions, done by many people, make a difference. They may also make jokes about other cultures without meaning harm; talk about how it feels to be laughed at.

title: فہمِ عبارت کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on comprehension passage (فہمِ عبارت), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Know how to read a passage carefully.
Read a passage and answer questions.
Learn the meanings of words in the passage.
Find answers in the passage.
Check facts from the passage.
Find synonyms and antonyms.
Write plurals of words from the passage.
Find the main idea of a passage.
Read a new passage and answer questions.
Write a short passage.

guide.what: Comprehension in Urdu (فہمِ عبارت): how to read a passage carefully, an original passage دادا جان کا باغ with questions, word meanings, finding answers, درست یا غلط, مترادف and متضاد, واحد جمع, finding the مرکزی خیال, a second passage سکول کی لائبریری, and writing a short passage.
steps: Read the passage aloud together, then ask your child to tell it back in their own words.
Ask questions that start with کون، کیا، کب، کہاں and کیوں.
Talk about the main idea of an Urdu story from the newspaper or a children's magazine.
home: Visit a garden or park and write four sentences about it in Urdu.
Make a family word list of opposites, like چھوٹا بڑا، صبح شام.
guide.watch: Children often answer from what they think instead of what the passage says. Teach them to underline the line where they found the answer. They may also write one-word answers; full sentences are expected.

title: Cyberbullying and kindness Practice
subject: ICT
desc: 10 pages of Grade 3 ICT practice on cyberbullying and kindness, from "What Is Cyberbullying?" to "My Kindness Pledge". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what cyberbullying is.
Tell kind and unkind online actions apart.
Understand how bullying makes people feel.
Know what to do if you are bullied online.
Know how to help someone who is being bullied.
Use THINK to check messages before posting.
Write kind messages.
Make safe and kind choices online.
Use maths with online kindness.
Plan to be kind and safe online.

guide.what: Cyberbullying and kindness: what cyberbullying is, kind and unkind online actions, how bullying feels, stop, save, block and tell, being an upstander, THINK before you post, writing kind messages, choosing what to do in real situations, and making a kindness pledge.
steps: Talk about the games and chats your child uses and who they talk to there.
Agree together who your child can tell if something online upsets them.
Practise blocking and reporting on a game or app together.
home: Send a kind message to a relative or friend as a family.
Make a THINK poster and stick it near the computer or tablet.
guide.watch: Children may think unkind messages are just jokes, or worry they will lose their tablet if they tell. Reassure them that telling a grown-up is always the right thing, and they will not be in trouble for it.
